articles.title_orig: Europe and China 1 – The Arrival of the People’s Republic - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
articles.title_zh: Europe and China 1 – The Arrival of the People’s Republic - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
articles.content_orig:
This is the first of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe.
In the 1990s, the shadow of Tiananmen Square fell across Europe’s trade relations with China. The massacre of protesters in 1989 marked a return to dictatorship and wiped out hopes of political reform. European firms drew back, an arms embargo was imposed, and political pressure grew to isolate “the butchers of Beijing.”
Yet by the end of the decade China had swept triumphantly into the World Trade Organisation (WTO), its economy was growing fast, and the world was at its door as a new word, “globalization,” set the agenda at every corporate summit.
To reconstruct the turnaround, a historian must first identify the political personalities behind it. Even as the blood was hosed off Tiananmen — and while the future President Xi Jinping’s wife, the singer Peng Liyuan, serenaded the martial law troops — many Chinese leaders knew they had made a terrible blunder.
They included Xi Jinping’s father, the twice-purged army veteran Xi Zhongxun, who paid homage in public to the “wise” and “resolute” decision to suppress “a counter-revolutionary riot” but in private mourned the setback to economic reform.
Xi Zhongxun himself had taken charge of the southern powerhouse of Guangdong, turning it into a workshop for the world that drew in foreign investment through the 1980s. He was one of the kingmakers who influenced the choice of China’s next leaders after 1989.
The new faces were two men who had stepped up from the coastal trading metropolis of Shanghai. Jiang Zemin, the Communist Party boss in Shanghai, a Soviet-trained engineer, became President and leader of the party. Yet the key figure turned out to be a dynamo called Zhu Rongji, the city’s mayor, a sharp-witted technocrat born in 1928. In succession, he became governor of the central bank and prime minister.
The duo had overseen a peaceful end to mass protests in China’s commercial capital at the time of Tiananmen. There was no massacre in Shanghai. Instead, Zhu went on television to issue a grim warning, and the authorities deployed police and militia to quieten the demonstrations slowly. Shanghai was soon back in business. European companies were in the first wave of investors in the city’s new financial district of Pudong.
Both leaders were determined to open China up to the world economy, defying vocal opposition from leftists in the party. Their campaign can be traced through the archives of the WTO in Geneva, an invaluable guide to the negotiations.
As early as 1986, China had applied to join the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), but the major trading powers had decided to transform the GATT into a new body that would govern services as well as trade from January 1, 1995.
It was too soon for China to join the new World Trade Organization at its birth, but negotiations began in earnest. The EU formed a negotiating bloc in rounds of bilateral talks between China and all its partners, which the WTO would then orchestrate into a package.
Accession was vital to China, as Zhu Rongji argued in party councils. In 1993, for example, the People’s Republic recorded a trade deficit of more than $12bn, due to the cost of imports for modernization. At the same time, China’s foreign trade had soared to $195bn from $20bn in 1978, the start of the “reform and open up” era.
John Bond, the chairman of HSBC Holdings, heard Zhu speak and realized that the Communist cadre had posed a modern version of the famous “Needham Question” raised by the Cambridge polymath, Joseph Needham, of why modern science had enjoyed a meteoric rise in Europe but not in China.
“How can 22% of the world’s population account for less than 4% of the world’s GNP?” Bond asked.
The WTO documents show the intricacy and the scale of that challenge. The rewards were obvious. In the five years after 1990, Guangdong Province, the former fiefdom of Xi Jinping’s father, saw an expansion across key industries of 40% every 12 months, according to the official Statistical Yearbook for 1996.
Formidable obstacles remained. Zhu Rongji fought battles in Beijing to push through a 1994 package of changes to banking, finance, taxation, investment, foreign exchange and foreign trade. The working party in Geneva met behind closed doors 21 times between March 1996 and September 2001.
The Europeans pressed hard on intellectual property, copyright protection, patents, trademarks (matters of great concern to Germany), test data, trade secrets, government procurement, minority shareholder rights, and judicial remedies. The WTO working party report alone ran to almost 200 pages. In the end, Europe had a deal.
The fate of China was put into American hands. Between September and December 2001, the Clinton administration waged cliff-edge negotiations with the Chinese that remain controversial to this day. A myth has grown that China was ushered into the WTO by vested interests pushing a globalization and free trade agenda. The record shows that China’s road to accession was, in fact, long, painstaking and hard-fought.
The final agreement imposed harsher conditions on China than any other nation when its membership became formal on December 11, 2001. It ran to 1,500 pages and weighed 13 kg (29 lbs.). Zhu Rongji saw his country become the world’s second largest economy, the biggest exporter, and the world’s largest holder of foreign currency reserves. He died earlier this year.
“It was win-win,’ said the Hong Kong representative in Geneva from 1994 to 2002, Stuart Harbinson. “That was the conventional wisdom.”
Michael Sheridan is a veteran British foreign correspondent and is the author of ‘ The Gate to China ’, an acclaimed history of Hong Kong, and ‘ The Red Emperor: Xi Jinping and His New China ’, which is published by Hachette Books and has been translated into a dozen languages, including Ukrainian, Polish, and Japanese.
Europe’s Edge is CEPA’s online journal covering critical topics on the foreign policy docket across Europe and North America. All opinions expressed on Europe’s Edge are those of the author alone and may not represent those of the institutions they represent or the Center for European Policy Analysis. CEPA maintains a strict intellectual independence policy across all its projects and publications.

articles.title_orig: Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of historic talks in China
articles.title_zh: Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of historic talks in China
articles.content_orig:
Watch: BBC correspondents discuss historic Trump, Xi and Putin meeting
Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for the first time in more than a year on Wednesday, as they prepared for landmark talks in China with Xi Jinping.
The US president was greeted off his plane by the Chinese leader as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting between the pair and the Russian president.
After a carefully choreographed handshake and hug between Trump and Xi on the tarmac, the US president later greeted and exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of a reception.
Trump and Putin are expected to hold one-on-one talks on the sidelines of the summit on Thursday, in which the war in Ukraine could be discussed.
However the main focus during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (Apec) will be on the US-China-Russia talks on Thursday - the first time the trio of leaders have met together in person.
A full agenda has not been made public but there have been various hints about what could be discussed, including the wars in Ukraine and Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions and developments in artificial intelligence.
After a warm reception from Xi, the leaders of the US and Russia shook hands ahead of a reception
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin and Trump have not yet held a substantive meeting, and merely greeted each other on Wednesday.
Peskov also said that "no more than an hour" had been allocated for Thursday's trilateral talks between Putin, Trump and Xi.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has raised fears of a plan to end the war being discussed in the absence of representatives from Kyiv or Europe.
It is unclear whether China would want this issue to be on the agenda in Shenzhen, with Beijing talking more generally about the need to discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability".
China has officially remained neutral since Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, rejecting accusations from Kyiv and its allies that it has been tacitly supporting Moscow, including by exporting dual-use technology used by the Russian military.
Wednesday's handshake was the first in-person meeting between Trump and Putin since August 2025, when the Russian leader travelled to Alaska for talks on the Ukraine war which failed to deliver a breakthrough.
Xi's personal reception for Trump at the airport mimicked a similar move by the US president when the Chinese leader visited Washington in September, a gesture Xi described as "special".
In Shenzhen, a red carpet was rolled out in front of Air Force One for Trump, with a cheering crowd, honour guard, military flyover and flowers presentation all in place to welcome him.
Chinese state-run news agency Xinhua quoted Xi as saying he wanted to pursue a "constructive strategic and stable relationship based on respect, fairness, and equality".
Xi's greeting will be seen as a diplomatic gesture designed to begin the week's talks with his American counterpart on a cordial note.
A lavish welcome ceremony was laid on for Trump's arrival
The south-east Chinese city the Apec summit is being held in is a booming area for manufacturing and advanced tech.
It comes against the backdrop of the ousting of Nvidia chief executing Jensen Huang, who admitted to having an affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence of spying for Beijing - a claim dismissed as a "smear" by China.
Trump has pursued warmer relations with China but the incident points to ongoing tensions between the two powers.
Several hours before Trump's arrival, Putin landed in Shenzhen and held around two hours of talks with Xi, with whom he has pressed for closer economic and defence relations.
Xi said both countries would "move forward steadily and boldly" and that the relationship was "stable as a mountain, unshaken by storms".

articles.title_orig: Nvidia halts China AI chip shipments despite US approval
articles.title_zh: Nvidia halts China AI chip shipments despite US approval
articles.content_orig:
Add Axios as your preferred source to
see more of our stories on Google.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at a May 2026 ceremony in China. Photo: Alex Wong/Getty Images
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday questioned whether Nvidia's earnings might have been inflated by inappropriate sales to China and urged the company to hire an outsider as CEO.
Why it matters: Nvidia is central to the AI economy, which has been key to U.S. economic growth.
Driving the news: In a Fox News appearance Sunday morning, Bessent said Nvidia owes the market an explanation amid allegations former CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a Chinese spy and oversaw sanctions-evading chip sales to Asian companies.
Bessent also said it was "obvious" that some companies doing business with Nvidia were shell companies for Chinese interests and accused the chipmaker of a "culture of noncompliance."
For the record: Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Bessent's remarks.
The intrigue: Huang has been a favorite of President Trump and other administration figures for some time, but Bessent has notably not been as effusive about him as others.
What to watch: Nvidia is due to report quarterly results on Tuesday, its first significant public comments since Huang resigned and CFO Collette Kress took over as acting CEO.

articles.title_orig: Wall Street prepares for Anthropic IPO frenzy, despite broader AI stock slump
articles.title_zh: Wall Street prepares for Anthropic IPO frenzy, despite broader AI stock slump
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic is considering upsizing its IPO, people familiar with the details told CNBC, as the artificial intelligence lab weighs setting the price well above $80.
The company closed its order books and locked in total demand on Tuesday, setting the stage for the Claude creator's eagerly awaited Nasdaq listing. Institutional demand for the offering is around $400 billion, while retail demand is approaching $100 billion, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly.
The orders are indications of interest and are not binding. All of the details are subject to change, and Anthropic will make final decisions on Wednesday afternoon, the people said. Anthropic is expected to set its final IPO price after market close on Wednesday.
Demand for the offering is higher than it was for Elon Musk's SpaceX , even though the rocket maker had a bigger market offering. SpaceX debuted on the Nasdaq in June in by far the biggest IPO on record, ultimately raising $85.7 billion.
The AI lab said last week that it would offer 825 million shares in the IPO at a price range between $70 and $78 per share, which would net up to $64.35 billion at the high end of that range.
A representative for Anthropic declined to comment.
Anthropic's listing is a major test for the AI industry, which has experienced a set of recent shocks, including a dramatic backlash that was felt at the polls in the midterm elections and last week's ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . The market was already jittery on concerns that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for many data center developers and neoclouds.
Tech's biggest companies have significant exposure to Anthropic, whether as an investor, partner or customer. Amazon and Google both own stakes valued at over $100 billion, and a group of tech companies, including Google, Microsoft , Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices agreed to collectively invest $26 billion in the IPO. Anthropic, meanwhile, is a buyer of costly systems from Nvidia, Google, Amazon and AMD.
"I think if we do this right, we can create an age of miracles where humanity is able to solve problems that have eluded us for millennia," Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in Anthropic's roadshow video . "We have to make sure that all the risks, all the ways that things can go wrong with this technology, we very carefully address those risks as we bring the benefits and as we have a viable business at the same time."
Amodei co-founded Anthropic alongside a handful of other researchers less than six years ago, after the group collectively defected from OpenAI. The company is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude , and it primarily sells its products and services to other businesses.
Anthropic has been racing to maintain an edge over OpenAI and Google in the enterprise market, and it experienced a period of explosive growth in 2026, driven largely by the popularity of its AI coding tool, Claude Code. OpenAI has confidentially filed for an IPO and has said a debut is likely in 2027.
For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said it generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year, according to its prospectus. The company reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said.
Anthropic said in an amended filing that its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the previous month.
The company has faced plenty of challenges during its meteoric rise over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, leading to two high-profile disputes with the U.S. government this year. Its prospectus included more than 90 pages of risk factors for investors to consider ahead of its IPO.
"Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the company's prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort."

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Dow Falls as Nvidia Earnings Fail to Soothe Investors' Nerves
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Dow Falls as Nvidia Earnings Fail to Soothe Investors' Nerves
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia’s leadership sought to set a path forward on Tuesday’s earnings call in the wake of former CEO Jensen Huang’s departure — defying calls to re-hire him, reassuring investors that demand for Nvidia’s products remains strong, and indicating that the leadership shakeup could prompt a new or more cautious approach to key elements of the company’s business.
The company has been rocked by scandal, national security concerns and the resignation of Huang, its founder and CEO of 33 years. And leadership was under pressure to reassure nervous investors Tuesday evening, with Nvidia having lost $751 billion in market value since last Sunday.
Many lingering questions remain. But investors appeared at least somewhat mollified by the comments and earnings results: shares ticked up nearly 5% in after-hours trading following the call.
Nvidia rules out Jensen Huang’s return as CEO, tells investors ‘we’ve got this’
Nvidia Board Chair Harvey Jones kicked off the earnings call by saying the board does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO, despite Huang’s statement earlier Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return should the board allow it.
Jones said the board has “every confidence” in CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress to lead the company as it searches for a permanent replacement. He added the board wants to install a permanent CEO “as quickly as possible,” but it wouldn’t rush to appoint someone until it finds “exactly the right person.”
The board is considering internal and external candidates for the role. And while Jones offered no further hints on who is under consideration, Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of Hyperscale and High-Performance Computing, joined Kress to take analyst questions on the call — a signal of his importance as a senior leader at the company.
Jones indicated that the board is taking the national security concerns into consideration in its search.
“The board appreciates that we’re living in a world where the advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace,” Jones said. “Our new CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully.”
Nvidia has played a key role in fueling the growth of the AI ecosystem by providing financing and investment to its customers to purchase its chips and build AI infrastructure.
Some industry analysts have questioned whether that will continue without Huang, who was considered the industry’s master dealmaker, even as others criticized the practice as “circular financing” that has artificially inflated the market.
Kress said on the call that the company has committed more than $100 billion to such deals as of the end of the quarter ended in October. However, she indicated that the company will carefully evaluate any deals to back would-be customers going forward.
“We remain thoughtful in how we participate and disciplined in how we commit capital,” Kress said. “We are proud of the role that we have played so far in supporting the ecosystem. As the market matures and additional sources of capital become available, we are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees.”
Beyond its existing deals, Nvidia will take “a very strong look in terms of the types of companies that we would want to help in terms of the financing,” she said.
The company earned $2.4 billion in sales of licensed chips to China during the third quarter — comprising just over 2% of the total revenue in its core data center business unit. But the company has ceased shipments to the country, Kress said during Tuesday’s call.
That news comes as the company faces increased scrutiny from US officials over the potential illicit transfer of its chips to China.
How the Nvidia scandal lifted the curtain on a loophole that’s giving China access to US chips
A complex network of loopholes of shell corporations and unauthorized brokers, often operating via countries like Singapore, are believed to have enabled the transfer of millions of Nvidia chips to China in violation of export controls. Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., estimated that China and Hong Kong “could comprise roughly 15%” of Nvidia’s previous revenues “when considering potential loopholes throughout Asia.”
The Commerce Department on Monday announced tighter export restrictions to prevent China from accessing sensitive, AI-powering computer chips via data centers in third-party countries.
The company is assuming no revenue from sales of licensed chips to China in the fourth quarter.
Even prior to Huang’s exit, questions were swirling about whether major tech companies might pull back on their spending on AI infrastructure as they face scrutiny from investors over when the technology will produce meaningful returns.
But Kress said demand for Nvidia’s products continues to outstrip supply, especially as a growing slate of companies and consumers seek to implement computing-intensive AI agents .
“Even in the last week, the continued ask is: How are we going to receive more and more supply to help (customers) with the demand that they have in front of them,” Kress said.
That growing demand pushed the company’s projection for full-year revenue growth in 2028 to 75%, up from its earlier projection of 70%. Nvidia also reported better-than-expected guidance for sales in the final quarter of this year.
“We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners,” following Huang’s resignation, Kress said. “They’re all 100% behind us.”

articles.title_orig: Dow slides 600 points, Nasdaq seesaws as Nvidia earnings bounce fizzles: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Dow slides 600 points, Nasdaq seesaws as Nvidia earnings bounce fizzles: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia shares sank around 2% Wednesday after the company issued its first earnings report since the departure of former CEO Jensen Huang .
Neoclouds bounced initially following the report before trading lower Wednesday. CoreWeave sank over 6%, Iren more than 4% and Nebius declined around 1%.
Nvidia's third-quarter revenue came in at $115.84 billion, more than $6 billion above analysts' expectations of $109.10 billion, while fourth-quarter guidance of $130 billion topped the $125.1 billion consensus, according to LSEG.
The semiconductor giant continues to navigate the fallout from Huang's resignation last week. Shortly before the results, Huang made his first public statement since resigning last week, saying that he was open to returning to the company, after an outpouring of support from prominent tech figures .
But Harvey Jones, the new and first-ever chair of Nvidia's board, said on the earnings call that the board does not intend to reinstate him as CEO.
″[Hyperscalers] are the ones that are right now feverishly looking for more focus in terms of the compute that we have available," interim CEO Colette Kress told Jim Cramer on CNBC's "Mad Money."
"This concept that anything is changing in terms of any of our types of customers — that is just not true. They are all continuing to be with us, and we have a very deep breath of different customers."
The U.S. Commerce Department announced a legal change on Monday to try and stem China's access to the most advanced Nvidia chips — which are already under export controls effectively preventing their import into the country — by restricting Chinese companies' ability to access compute remotely in overseas data centers.
Nvidia told investors in its earnings commentary that it was "not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in our outlook," in keeping with its recent language on the country.
— CNBC's Caleigh Keating contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: I watched Trump, Xi and Putin gather in China. Here are my top takeaways
articles.title_zh: I watched Trump, Xi and Putin gather in China. Here are my top takeaways
articles.content_orig:
SHENZHEN, China — It took a trip to China for me, an American, to see U.S. President Donald Trump in person for the first time.
Trump emerged from a group of black-clad photographers and other personnel surrounding him at a welcome banquet in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting held November 17th to 19th.
Seated just a few spots to his left was Russian President Vladimir Putin who picked up a glass of red wine to join a toast led by Chinese President Xi Jinping .
"At tomorrow's Leaders' Meeting, we will discuss measures to expand mutual opening up, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, and identify opportunities to expand practical cooperation across various fields, so as to translate more initiatives into tangible results," Xi said in Mandarin, according to a CNBC translation.
Xi was speaking broadly, but Thursday's agenda includes a bilateral meeting with Trump, and their highly anticipated trilateral meeting with Putin.
But looking at the mood in the room, it seemed that their trilateral conversation had already started Wednesday night at their long banquet table. Much of what happens at APEC, including bilateral meetings and other exchanges between leaders, takes place away from the media.
But what struck me was how little sign there was of the tension surrounding Nvidia 's CEO Jensen Huang resignation, a controversy that has gripped markets for the past 10 days.
Ahead of Trump's entrance into the banquet hall, Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao shared a friendly moment with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other members of the American delegation.
Last week, the U.S. officials said that Trump did not plan to raise allegations of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy during his meeting with Xi.
It was a striking contrast to just two months ago, when I saw photographs of Huang and Tesla CEO Elon Musk sharing a table with Trump and Xi in Washington, D.C.
And when Trump visited Beijing in May, Huang took a few minutes to speak with reporters, including me, inside the Great Hall of the People. Musk was there too, accompanied by one of his sons.
This time, neither were visible in a room that was closely watched by the world. Musk was expected to join Trump's delegation in Shenzhen, but I did not see him Wednesday evening.
Their absence from the government-heavy banquet was striking. The world's most powerful leaders may be grappling with the implications of artificial intelligence, but they certainly didn't need the industry's biggest names at the table to do so.
China's Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers
Putin says EU is losing industry, falling behind competition
Three things to watch as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
Over the months I've spent following APEC's "China Year," one thing has become clear: The forum has given Beijing an opportunity to host the U.S., Japan and other member economies at a time when unresolved tensions might otherwise have made such gatherings difficult.
But even in a year defined by talks of U.S.-China "strategic stability," the APEC events have exposed the rifts and the shifting dynamics in global power. Those dynamics were on display for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.
Several hundred attendees, from Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun to U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue, arrived early for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.
After waiting in silence for at least 10 minutes, the audience welcomed Xi in a distinctly modern way: by raising their smartphones to capture the moment. The applause was rather muted.
It was much the same at the more government-heavy welcome banquet that evening. So many attendees rushed to take their own photographs of Xi and other leaders entering the room that reporters' views were largely blocked.
Following Xi's morning speech, there was a lengthy intermission before Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim took the stage.
"The entire multilateral framework needs to change," he said, praising China on its "rare" recognition of smaller countries.
During the tea break that followed, attendees quickly resumed mingling. Some even brought coffee and snacks back into the room as Putin prepared to speak.
They listened as the Russian president talked about his country's economic resilience and claimed Europe was losing ground. As attendees headed to lunch, one thing stood out: Neither Trump nor any other G7 leader had taken the stage at the opening event. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke later in the afternoon.
The most visible American presence during the morning session came from business leaders appearing in a promotional video ahead of Xi's speech.
And the absence of an American voice was perhaps even more noticeable at Wednesday evening's banquet.
Trump did not follow Xi with a toast of his own. This was the same famously outspoken president, who in a winding speech in Davos, had declared that the U.S. must get Greenland .
Yet on Wednesday night in China, Trump wasn't the one holding the microphone.

articles.title_orig: US Stocks Rise as Nvidia Outlook Tempers AI Fears: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: US Stocks Rise as Nvidia Outlook Tempers AI Fears: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
Five days after Nvidia 's Jensen Huang resigned from the company he co-founded 33 years ago under a cloud of scandal, a nervous base of shareholders eagerly awaited Colette Kress' first public appearance as interim CEO.
Following Nvidia's better-than-expected earnings report on Tuesday, Kress offered some relief to Wall Street, at least temporarily, by proclaiming on the call with analysts that customers are still fully onboard and that there's no slippage in demand. She said leadership from Nvidia's most important supplier, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company , visited company offices this week.
"We've engaged with our customers, we've engaged with our suppliers, our partners, they're all 100% behind us," Kress said on the call. "Customers have expressed their support to the business outlook and helping us through that."
While Huang was a singular figure in artificial intelligence with a commanding presence across the globe, Nvidia is still at the center of the AI ecosystem. Customers ranging from hyperscalers and neoclouds to frontier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic remain in persistent need of its technology and capital.
Nvidia shares climbed almost 5% in extended trading on Tuesday after the chipmaker's better-than-expected earnings and strong guidance. That still leaves the stock in a deep slump after a 24% drop so far this month, driven by broad concerns about a slowdown in the AI buildout, a political handoff in Washington, D.C., and the turmoil at the top of the company.
Despite all those headwinds and what Nvidia called the "unexpected transition" in leadership, the business is still booming. Revenue more than doubled in the latest quarter to $115.84 billion, and Nvidia projects roughly 90% growth in the current period to about $130 billion.
More importantly, Kress said the 70% growth forecast for next year that was offered over the summer is actually too low. Now the projection is 75%. That's for a company that's seen revenue multiply by about 15-fold since the launch of ChatGPT in late 2022.
While Huang is gone, "demand did not leave with him," Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives said in a note after the report.
Kress maintained her optimistic tone in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer after the call.
"The most important thing that we have been seeing is continuing growth in terms of the demand that's out there," she said.
Kress also said on the call that Nvidia's stepped-up buybacks, announced in September, are still on track, confirming that the board had added $150 billion to the company's authorization for share repurchases.
It's not all on Kress. The consistent message throughout the earnings call was that Nvidia is preparing for life after Huang.
Harvey Jones, the newly named chair of Nvidia's board, opened by saying that Huang had resigned after "disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms," the first time the board had given a reason for his removal.
A day earlier, CNBC reported that Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back as CEO.
Kress said on the call that it's "business as usual." In a statement, she said the company's roadmap is "on track," indicating that there haven't been any changes to future chips and systems currently in development. Nvidia said that the Vera Rubin AI system is off to an "extraordinary start," selling $20 billion in the latest quarter.
But Kress did signal a slight change to the company's willingness to backstop certain projects, and said Nvidia is being "disciplined" with how it's thinking about financing startups.
"There's a lot of discussion internally with a lot of the teams on what we think are the best ones that we want to do," Kress told Cramer. "We're going to continue down that path to make sure we choose the right investments for us to work through going forward,"
Plenty of big questions remain.
Nvidia said its quarterly filing would be published in the "coming weeks," whereas it normally lands on the same day as earnings. On the call, neither Kress nor Jones addressed an avalanche of investigations and hearings in Washington looking into allegations that Nvidia was boosting revenue by selling chips to companies that are passthroughs for buyers in China.
China only came up twice during the call. Kress said Nvidia had sold about $2.4 billion worth of approved data center products to China during the quarter, and that Nvidia had stopped selling licensed Hopper chips to China.
Kress also noted that new trade rules released by the U.S. Commerce Department will cut off Chinese access to renting Nvidia chips.
None of that is stunting growth.
"Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us and employees are committed," Kress said when signing off the call. "We've got this."

Apple is reportedly planning a major redesign for its 20th-anniversary iPhone 20 Pro lineup next year, with quad-curved displays and several other improvements. A new leak has now revealed more details about the upcoming models.
Tipster Ice Universe shared the latest details about the 20th-anniversary iPhones on X, claiming that Apple is developing four models for next year.
Two of the models will feature flat cover glass, while the other two will sport the much-rumored quad-curved design. Apple has reportedly been developing the new design for around three years, making several revisions along the way.
According to Ice Universe, early prototypes had deeper curves, which were later toned down. The tipster also claims that the quad-curved glass shown in a recently leaked video belonged to an early prototype.
The models with quad-curved glass are said to have 1mm bezels. However, the curvature is said to make them almost invisible when viewed straight on. Ice Universe also claims that industry insiders are more excited about the upcoming anniversary iPhones than the recently launched iPhone Duo .

articles.title_orig: Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard lore
articles.title_zh: Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard lore
articles.content_orig:
Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard lore
The latest Arcane Journal, The Doom of Lord Carrard , will be available to pre-order this weekend. To find out more, we undertook our own quest into the depths of the Warhammer studio to speak to the designers about the lore of the latest supplement.
JTY: Since the release of Warhammer: The Old World, we’ve been following the events of Settra the Imperishable’s war against the Old World. We’ve seen his armies advance through the Border Princes and navigate the peaks and valleys of the Vaults en route to the borders of Bretonnia. We’ve even seen what happens when an ancient Liche Priest leads an army of the Undead into the depths of Athel Loren . But what we haven’t covered in much detail is what caused all this turmoil in the first place.
In Arcane Journal – the Doom of Lord Carrard we decided to address this. We wanted to explore the charnel realm of Nehekhara in greater detail, and we felt Lord Carrard’s quest allowed us to do just that.
Much of the narrative is told from the perspective of the Bretonnians, giving us a relatable lens through which to view the horrors of the Land of the Dead. This allowed us to introduce Lord Carrard himself, a baron from the realm of Brionne, and establish his relationship with Sir Lothar of Kasos Rock, once a noble knight of Carrard’s court but now an outcast dwelling in the Border Princes .
It is the arrival of a messenger from Sir Lothar that sets in motion the events that are to follow. Bringing the grim forebodings from Sir Lothar’s court, the messenger warns of a great evil stirring in the Land of the Dead and implores Lord Carrard for his aid in vanquishing it. Rather than muster armies on the strength of vague portents, the baron elects to undertake a quest, riding in the company of his closest companions to the court of his former friend.
The next part of the story is told through the recollections of Sir Varo, one of the few to return and bring word of Lord Carrard’s fate, and of the evil that has been awakened in the Land of the Dead. Through Varo we learn of the Bretonnians’ journey to the accursed city of Zandri, from where we explore Nehekhara itself, coming face to face with the horrors of the Land of the Dead as the bold knights cross the deserts and battle the undead horrors placed before them. Accompanied by a wealth of stunning new art, this tale casts a whole new light upon this accursed realm, giving the reader a sense of the scale of the civilisation that once ruled the deserts of the Great Land, and the horrors a traveller might encounter in deserts haunted by looming horrors beneath skies shrouded behind impregnable dust storms.
But that’s not all. Arcane Journal – The Doom of Lord Carrard also examines ancient Nehekhara, in particular the major cities of that once-vibrant land, and the royal dynasties that once ruled over them. Delving into such ancient history was a fun challenge, and reading about the cities and dynasties of the Land of the Dead will hopefully inspire readers. There are lots of ideas here for theming your own collections of Tomb Kings of Khemri to reflect the armies of a particular city or monarch.
It’s always fun to explore the World of Legend, and shining a light on the events that led to Settra's climactic invasion was especially enjoyable. This was a story we were keen to tell, and we can’t wait to see how it will inspire readers!
Thanks, JTY! The new Arcane Journal is available for pre-order from Saturday, along with a wealth of reinforcements for the Tomb Kings of Khemri in the form of Skeleton Warriors , Skeleton Archers, Horsemen and Horse Archers , and Skeleton Chariots. Join us later in the week when we’ll be learning more about the rules in the Arcane Journal.

articles.title_orig: Iran Attacks Kuwait and Bahrain, Further Escalating Fight Over Strait
articles.title_zh: Iran Attacks Kuwait and Bahrain, Further Escalating Fight Over Strait
articles.content_orig:
CAIRO (AP) — Iran widened its attacks on its Gulf neighbors on Wednesday, targeting a US air base in Kuwait and launching several attacks on Bahrain in what appeared to be retaliation for American strikes the day before.
After about two months without such attacks, Iran has repeatedly targeted US facilities in Bahrain in recent days. The small Persian Gulf island kingdom hosts the US Navy’s 5th Fleet.
The early morning attacks came after a US fighter jet struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site Tuesday on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The US strike was in retaliation for an Iranian attack on an American radar installation in Bahrain earlier Tuesday.
Iran said that its recent attacks — including those on other US facilities in Bahrain on Sunday and Friday — were in response to US drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers.
The uptick in fighting with the tit-for-tat attacks raises the risk of further escalation toward the resumption of all-out conflict nearly nine months into the war, and complicates negotiations for a diplomatic solution, which have stagnated despite intensified mediation efforts from Qatar.
The US military didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment on the latest attacks.
With its economy suffering under a US naval blockade and American military escorts helping restore the passage of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, experts say that the recent attacks suggest Tehran may be growing weary of the status quo.
“Even if neither side intends to enter a broader confrontation, the accumulation of military incidents across multiple fronts increases the risk of miscalculation and escalation beyond what either side originally intended,” Hamidreza Azizi, senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group think tank, wrote in an analysis posted to X following the initial reports of the attack on Kuwait.
US President Donald Trump has sent mixed messages on his next steps, saying new strikes are highly unlikely, but also sending a third aircraft carrier and thousands more troops to the Middle East.
Though US military protection has helped restore oil shipments from the Gulf, Iran has continued to attack tankers as they attempt to transit the Strait of Hormuz.
United Arab Emirates state-owned oil company ADNOC said Wednesday that one of its tanker crew members was missing after an attack in the strait on Tuesday, while 11 others were injured and were receiving medical care.
Danny Citrinowicz, a researcher at Israel’s Institute for National Security Studies and a former Iran specialist in Israel’s military and intelligence services, described an “increasingly clear” pattern of attacks by Iran on shipping and US facilities in the Gulf region.
“Iran appears to be pursuing a strategy of deliberate, calibrated escalation,” he wrote in an analysis on X. “The objective is not necessarily to trigger an all-out war, but to steadily increase the military, economic, and political costs of maintaining the blockade.”
He said that Washington is faced with the dilemma that a limited response may encourage Iran to push further, while a stronger response risks accelerating the escalation that the US is trying to avoid.
“As long as the US naval blockade remains in place and no agreement is reached, further escalation will become increasingly difficult to avoid,” he said. “There are two clear paths to de-escalation: a negotiated agreement or a US decision to lift the blockade.”
After Israel and the US attacked Iran on Feb. 28 to launch the war, Iran regularly fired on American facilities and interests in neighboring Gulf countries, as well as energy infrastructure and other targets.
In the attack early Wednesday on the Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait, the Iranian military fired at air defense systems and drone and missile launch platforms, according to a report on Iran’s state broadcaster.
Kuwait’s military said that its air defenses had intercepted drone attacks and didn’t immediately report any damage. The Kuwaiti Foreign Ministry condemned the repeated Iranian attacks as “criminal,” saying that they threatened the country’s security and stability.
During the war, Ali Al Salem Air Base has been struck at least 30 times by Iran, damaging or destroying at least 15 aircraft hangars, numerous warehouses and 10 buildings near a residential area, according to an analysis by The Associated Press.
The AP’s analysis used satellite imagery from multiple providers to help determine that Iran’s strikes on more than two dozen US bases in the Middle East focused on early-warning systems before hitting aircraft and buildings, causing billions of dollars in equipment damage.
AP also spoke to four regional officials who were briefed or had firsthand knowledge of what was hit. The AP found that, through August, more than 115 drone or missile strikes claimed by Iran or Iranian-backed militias damaged or destroyed structures on 26 military bases and other sites with US equipment.
Under questioning before a US Senate committee Tuesday about damage to the Navy’s regional headquarters in Bahrain, Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said he couldn’t offer a full damage assessment in Bahrain because “it’s a nonpermissive area for us to go.” He told a reporter months ago that Iran “blew the hell out of Bahrain.”
Meanwhile, Bahrain’s Interior Ministry issued two alerts early Wednesday urging people to take shelter, followed by the “all clear” a short time later. The country’s military later said that it had intercepted a number of attacks from Iran, but gave no information on any damage or casualties.
Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed two cruise missiles fired toward the capital, Riyadh, by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen, according to Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki, spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis. Alerts also sounded in three other Saudi cities. Civil defense authorities later said that the danger had passed, but provided no further details.
The previous day, coalition forces launched a major air attack across rebel-held areas of Yemen that the Houthis said killed at least 17 people.
Al-Malki said that Tuesday’s strikes destroyed “60 legitimate military targets” and aimed to weaken the Houthis’ missile and drone capabilities.
The strikes followed the withdrawal of Saudi-backed forces from areas around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a setback for the anti-Houthi camp. The withdrawal consolidated the Houthis’ grip on the strategic waterway, which is crucial to international trade and global oil shipments.
Rising reported from Bangkok.

articles.title_orig: EU proposes €45 billion Ukraine loan, to be repaid after Russia pays reparations
articles.title_zh: EU proposes €45 billion Ukraine loan, to be repaid after Russia pays reparations
articles.content_orig:
(From L) European Council President Antonio Costa, President Volodymyr Zelensky and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen speak to the press upon arriving to attend an EU summit in Brussels on Oct. 16, 2026. (Nicolas Tucat / AFP via Getty Images)
BRUSSELS, Belgium — The European Commission is set to propose an additional 45 billion euros ($49.5 billion) in loans to Ukraine in 2027, and legal tweaks to unlock billions more from other countries, according to a draft document seen by the Kyiv Independent on Nov. 17.
The draft proposal, set to be presented on Nov. 18, comes after President Volodymyr Zelensky revealed in October that Ukraine would have a 70 billion-euro ($77 billion) shortfall in 2027 alone and called on the EU to help.
The Commission proposes to generate 45 billion euros in loans "guaranteed by the EU budget headroom," reads the draft document. The new proposal would then be put forward for discussion and approval by EU member states.
"Ukraine would only repay once it receives reparations from Russia," reads the draft document, the same condition as applied to the previously approved 90 billion euro ($99 billion) loan , which is partway through being disbursed.
As with the previous loan, the proposal suggests dividing the 45 billion euros into three funding pipelines.
The largest share, 25 billion euros ($27.5 billion), would fund defense industry capacity in Ukraine and be handed out in return for Ukraine submitting product schedules, essentially shopping lists of what it wants to buy.
As with the 90 billion-euro loan, EU and Ukrainian manufacturers would be prioritized, but an agile approval mechanism would be retained to allow third-country purchases when needed.
Ukraine has already used this mechanism to get exemptions for cheap Chinese drone components and U.S.-made PAC-3 Patriot interceptor missiles , where European producers are not able to provide viable alternatives at the speed and scale required.
The remaining 20 billion euros ($22 billion), as per the draft document, will be split equally between two buckets that pay Ukraine in exchange for implementing EU and IMF reforms: "Macro-Financial Assistance" and the "Ukraine Facility."
But that still leaves 25 billion euros of Zelensky's originally projected shortfall unaccounted for.
Throughout 2026, the European Commission reiterated that the 90 billion-euro loan was designed to cover only two-thirds of Ukraine's needs and that third countries need to step up .
To avoid the same pitfall, the Commission's proposal suggests changes to two laws to make it easier for allies to increase their support for Ukraine.
One change involves amending the Ukraine Facility, the pot of money that rewards Kyiv for passing reforms required to become an EU member, so that "third countries of high credit quality … provide irrevocable, unconditional, and on-demand financial guarantees" to the EU.
The guarantees could unlock an additional 5 billion euros ($5.5 billion) for the Ukraine Facility, supplementing the 10 billion euros ($11 billion) already proposed by the EU, according to the document.
The proposal also envisages that those countries would help pay the interest on the debt with an "appropriate contribution," but these payments going through the EU mechanism would be lower than if they were to simply assist Ukraine bilaterally.
Norway has already contributed to the Ukraine Facility , suggesting there might be appetite for other countries to opt in to this plan.
The second proposal involves amending a law to "support G7 members in providing new loans to Ukraine," which the document calls "second generation ERA loans."
The first generation of ERA loans was agreed in October 2024 and made $50 billion available to Ukraine, with the loans serviced and repaid using profits generated by Russian immobilized state assets.
Per the Commission proposal, "such new loans would be repaid from future flows of extraordinary revenues stemming from the immobilization of Russian sovereign assets … once the initially supported loans have been paid."
But the document does not predict exactly how much new money that idea would unlock.
The Commission's proposal is an attempt to square a circle, which, as Russia's war drags on, is increasingly hard to do in a pain-free way.
The document acknowledges that "the mobilization of additional significant resources by Member States to be able to finance Ukraine would constitute an important economic challenge."
The costs of bolstering defense spending, maintaining support for Ukraine, hastening the switch to renewable energy, and servicing welfare states in aging countries are all contributing to budget strain across the EU.
All but four EU countries are projected to have budget deficits in 2027 according to economic forecasts published on Nov. 17.
Belgium's coalition government is on the brink of collapse as it struggles to reach a compromise on how to turn around its financial situation.
And countries on the Eastern Flank have been saying they should receive more EU support in the next budget because they shoulder a disproportionate share of the burden of defending the bloc and policing its borders.
"It is appropriate to develop an innovative solution that is not expected to place a financial burden on either Ukraine or Member States," reads the draft Commission document.
But the draft regulation also foresees the EU paying down the costs of the new 45 billion-euro loan, just as it does for the already approved 90 billion-euro loan, using the "headroom" of the EU budget.
EU countries are still negotiating the bloc's next seven-year budget (for 2028-2034). As it stands, it includes a proposed 89 billion euros ($98 billion) in support for Ukraine.
That figure is not enough to cover Ukraine's shortfall for even one year, and the cost of servicing existing loans would be expected to significantly eat into it.
At that point, other options will need to be considered, some of them unpalatable, assuming support for Ukraine should continue.
For example, EU countries could hand over more of their tax revenue or raise taxes, both of which politicians will be reluctant to do, as many EU countries are set to hold elections in 2027.
The bloc could revisit the appropriation of over 200 billion euros ($220 billion) in Russian state assets held within the EU, a move opposed by several countries, most notably Belgium, when it was floated in December 2025.
Representatives of several EU countries have told the Kyiv Independent that there is still no appetite to revisit the topic, and that the underlying issues remain the same, despite efforts by EU lawmakers and several countries to relaunch the idea.
Other ideas could yet gain traction, such as the Windfall Optimization Loan Framework (WOLF), which promises to maximize profits from Russian assets without changing their legal status.
But so far EU countries have not grappled seriously with that or other ideas.
The first chance for EU leaders to discuss the Commission's proposal and how to finance Ukraine for the long haul will be at a meeting of the European Council in Brussels, scheduled for Nov. 26-27.
Hopes are high that agreement on funding Ukraine for 2027 and the next EU budget as a whole can be reached in time for the final EU leaders' meeting of the year, scheduled for Dec. 17-18.
Hi, this is Chris Powers. Thanks for reading this article. The EU is a famously complicated beast to understand, but for Ukraine, it has also never been as important.
Whether it's Russia sanctions, fighting corruption, or the process of joining the EU itself, many Kyivan roads eventually pass through Brussels.
If you like reading about these fiendishly complex topics and want to support journalists in Kyiv and Brussels to shine a light on it all, please consider supporting The Kyiv Independent.

articles.title_orig: Devolver Digital wants you to delete GTA 6 for a chance to win a free game
articles.title_zh: Devolver Digital wants you to delete GTA 6 for a chance to win a free game
articles.content_orig:
Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.
Devolver Digital has always had something of a reputation
        amongst game publishers as a wild card, a cheeky band who will take
        unusual, often silly measures to promote their upcoming games. Said
        measures can range from creating entire standalone games like Devolverland Expo to hitching a ride on whatever the current
        trend is in pop culture, and whether or not they work, you have to
        respect the publisher’s sheer commitment to the bit.
Now, if I asked you, “what’s the biggest buzz in pop culture right now,” the answer would undoubtedly be Grand Theft Auto 6 . The game is finally launching in two days after over a decade of
        development, and everyone who plans on playing has likely had their
        preloads locked and loaded since they opened up last week. However,
        here’s the big question: would you be willing to part with all 212 GB of that preload for a chance to win a copy of a pixel art sidescroller?
On the official Devolver Digital X , formerly Twitter account , the publisher announced its latest marketing stunt: an official
        giveaway contest for its next upcoming title, Volvy’s Adventure: Reslimed , which just so happens to be
        launching the same day as GTA 6 on November 19. Do you want to
        win? All you have to do is bin your preload.
As Devolver Digital explains in its X post, it’s
        offering the chance to win a free copy of Volvy Adventure: Reslimed to anyone who reposts with the
        hashtag “#MakeRoomForVolvy,” alongside a clip of them deleting their GTA 6 preload from their console. Said clip can either be
        direct captured footage from the console in question, or just a filmed
        clip taken with your phone, but either way, that preload has to go
        bye-bye if you want a chance to win.
A follow-up post notes that Volvy’s Adventure is exclusively
        launching for PC, so while the filmed clip does need to be of a preload
        deletion on a console, you will need a PC to actually redeem and play
        the game through Steam if you win.
That preload has to go bye-bye if you want a chance to win.
Obviously, the contest doesn’t require you to skip playing GTA 6 altogether; you can immediately preload the game again
        after deleting it, and Devolver won’t care. You just have to
        show your commitment to the bit, and considering the game’s massive
        preload has reportedly taken some users several days to download, that’s
        a bigger commitment for some than others.
Even so, the contest has drawn some interest, with a number of
        retweeters deleting their preloads in the name of Volvy , though
        others have apparently already pre-ordered Volvy’s Adventure on Steam and weren’t planning on getting GTA 6 anyway.
        Life is funny like that sometimes.
The release of Grand Theft Auto 6 isn’t just a product launch,
        it’s a full-on social phenomenon. Everyone is talking about it, even
        those completely outside of the gaming culture sphere, and businesses
        around the world are bracing for large swaths of their employees to
        spontaneously develop the flu on release day to skip work.
Not dissimilar to Devolver , many other businesses in and out of
        the gaming industry are looking for their own ways to capitalize on this
        major pop culture moment. Just today, KFC ’s Australian branch announced it would be holding a fake funeral to give people an excuse to call out
        of work, alongside offering free delivery throughout the country on
        launch day.
Similarly, DJ Khaled is running a promotion alongside XBOX where he’s signing sick day notes under the guise of “Dr.
        XBOX,” warning that many people are experiencing a severe “vitamin G
        deficiency.”
I’m honestly uncertain whether this mass marketing push will slow once GTA 6 actually comes out, or just ramps up further, at least
        for a month or so afterward.

articles.title_orig: Israeli tanks roll into central Gaza in first ground operation since ceasefire began
articles.title_zh: Israeli tanks roll into central Gaza in first ground operation since ceasefire began
articles.content_orig:
Israeli tanks advanced in an area of ​the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, witnesses said, and the Israeli military said its forces were targeting Hamas infrastructure outside areas that Israel controls in ⁠the enclave.
Witnesses said some Israeli tanks rolled onto the main Salahudeen road, west of the Yellow Line that marks the boundary of the two-thirds of the Gaza Strip still under Israeli control despite ⁠a ceasefire that has ​lasted more ⁠than a year.
An Israeli airstrike near the army raid killed one person, Palestinian medics said.
The medics ⁠said separate Israeli airstrikes had killed two other people ​earlier ⁠in the day in ‌ Deir al-Balah and Gaza City.
An Israeli military spokesperson told NBC News that the military was carrying out an operation targeting “Hamas infrastructure” west of ‌the Yellow Line in central Gaza ‌and that it had struck a militant in southern Gaza earlier on Wednesday.
The lates confirmed that it was the first ground operation since the U.S. brokered ceasefire came into effect in October 2025 .
The truce halted major fighting in the Israel-Gaza war although it has not stopped Israeli attacks or secured Hamas’ disarmament.
The spokesperson had no immediate comment on other strikes.
Israel, which says Hamas has recently been regrouping and rearming, has stepped up attacks against the Islamist group. Hamas has accused Israel of attempting to derail the U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement.
Gaza health ‌authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been ​killed since the ceasefire went into effect, while ‌the Israeli military says five Israeli soldiers have been killed.
Palestinian authorities say more ⁠than 74,000 people in Gaza have been killed in the military campaign ‌that Israel ​launched there after Hamas-led fighters killed ‌about 1,200 people in southern ​Israel in an attack on October 7, 2023.
Chantal Da Silva reports on world news for NBC News Digital and is based in London.

articles.title_orig: Hims & Hers launches new peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy
articles.title_zh: Hims & Hers launches new peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy
articles.content_orig:
Hims & Hers Health on Wednesday said it will offer five formulations of peptides and longevity treatments compounded in the U.S. as part of the initial rollout of its Peptides+ platform, all of which are not approved by regulators.
Even as it announced the new products, Hims & Hers acknowledged it has more to learn about how best to use the peptides and how effective they are — underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the growing space.
The new offerings come after the federal government eased restrictions on compounding certain unapproved peptides, which are short chains of amino ​acids. Those products have exploded in popularity among fitness and longevity enthusiasts who attest that they help with muscle growth, rapid injury recovery and anti-aging, even though most lack evidence from robust human trials.
Hims in late October launched an early access list for the upcoming peptide offerings, and more than 10,000 people signed up within 15 days, a company spokesperson said in a statement.
None of the company's specific compounded products are approved by the Food and Drug Administration. But Hims said they are authorized by law and formulated by pharmacies "that adhere to rigorous quality standards and are licensed and inspected by state boards of pharmacy."
The products include compounded formulations of sermorelin, a peptide that stimulates growth-hormone release and is marketed for recovery, body composition and anti-aging; glutathione, a peptide promoted ‌for anti-aging and athletic recovery; and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, or NAD+, a coenzyme that plays a role in cellular metabolism.
The company will also offer compounded versions of vitamin B-12, a vitamin needed to make red blood cells, build DNA, and maintain healthy nerve function, and L-carnitine, an amino acid derivative that helps the body turn fat into energy. The FDA has approved certain prescription forms of both peptides for established medical uses, primarily for diagnosed deficiencies in those compounds.
Hims said it plans to add more peptides and therapies made in the U.S. over time. That includes BPC-157, an unapproved peptide derived from a protein found in human gastric juice that is marketed for healing processes. The company also aims to introduce another unapproved peptide called TB-500, which is derived from a naturally occurring protein in the body and is marketed for broader, systemic soft-tissue recovery and flexibility. Most of the research on both has been conducted in animals, not humans.
To receive the products, members on the Hims platform will start with an assessment of health history and goals with a licensed provider trained in peptide therapies, who can tailor a personalized plan to their needs, if appropriate.
The company said it intends to use its communication platform to check in with patients and ensure they are seeing desired results.
"If they're not, we need to do something about it," Dr. Anant Vinjamoori, Hims chief medical officer, told CNBC. "We need to, you know, adjust the dose when that's appropriate, or in some cases consider other compounds that's maybe a better fit. And of course, there will also be cases when we need to refer people to other care options."
However, Vinjamoori said there's still uncertainty over how to best use the peptides.
"We don't have all of this data that we're used to having with compounds like this," he said. "We have the opportunity to get it right, and I think we see that as our responsibility with a company of our size, our skill, and resources to really lead."
Vinjamoori added that people who have serious illnesses, such as cardiovascular disease, liver disease and kidney disease, will not be candidates for the compounds for now.
Meanwhile, Andrew Huberman, a well known neuroscientist, podcaster and Stanford University School of Medicine professor who recently joined Hims' board of directors, in a statement called compounds "real medical treatments, not just a wellness trend." He said Hims provides safe access through "trusted sourcing and physician oversight."
But health experts raised concerns about the broader mainstream marketing of peptides in the U.S. and accessing them on telehealth platforms.
"With peptides, I think you have to view them the same way you would view any drug that hasn't been rigorously tested," said Joshua Kritzer, a chemistry professor at Tufts University. "Without actual testing, all you have is anecdotal information, and that's just not enough information to put a substance in your body."
Kritzer said the lack of large clinical trials means researchers can't rule out potentially serious, rare complications from peptides — the kinds of risks that have led regulators to reject or pull otherwise effective drugs from the market after they underwent comprehensive testing in humans.
Without that testing, it's also unclear how telehealth firms, physicians and pharmacies can make decisions about what doses patients should take, said Paul Knoepfler, a cell biology and human anatomy professor at UC Davis Health. While some people rely on anecdotal data from real peptide users, "the dosing for these products really has not been established," he added.
Knoepfler said one risk is that injecting too much of a synthetic peptide into patients could trigger "weird immune responses that are really bad for one's health" because the body might recognize it as foreign.
"With the peptides, it's very loosey-goosey," Knoepfler told CNBC. "How does one even know what would be the effective amount for whatever you're hoping it will do, and what amount would have more risks?"
But he said the more contact patients can have with physicians around taking a compounded peptide, the better. Providers, including those tied to telehealth firms, should make sure patients are well-informed about the possible risks and unknowns of a given product and consider their preexisting conditions, cancer history and other medications, Knoepfler said.
That appears to be consistent with the approach Hims & Hers is taking. The company says patients who use the peptide and longevity products can also use its Care+ offering, which pairs treatment with ongoing support. That includes twice-a-year lab testing to track their progress and the ability to message providers trained in peptide therapy around the clock with any questions.
Still, Kritzer argued that having a doctor who only knows a patient from online, essentially mail-order platforms or websites "is not enough supervision to put you on a prescription medication," especially an unapproved one.
Hims' ability to legally sell some of these peptides stems from a major shift in federal oversight by the Health and Human Services Department. It issued a policy in October that says the Food and Drug Administration will not take enforcement action against licensed pharmacies, federal facilities or physicians that compound and dispense six unapproved peptides while formal rules are reviewed.
In practice, that means these pharmacies and other firms can now offer them, even though the peptides aren't yet on the FDA's official list of ingredients compounding pharmacies are allowed to make. It does not translate to formal approval of the specific peptides.
The policy followed a 2023 decision by the Biden administration where the FDA restricted compounding pharmacies from producing popular peptide formulations due to safety, impurity and immune-reaction concerns.
HHS Secretary ​Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has supported broader access to peptides, calling himself a "big fan" of the treatments and arguing that restrictions were driving Americans to potentially unsafe products from overseas. Kennedy has previously described using BPC-157 to treat a muscle injury.
The announcement also comes after Hims in February 2025 acquired a California-based peptide manufacturing facility equipped with advanced peptide synthesizers.
The evidence for peptide efficacy varies by compound.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia’s RTX Spark Desktops Imagine They Can Actually Compete With the Mac Studio
articles.title_zh: Nvidia’s RTX Spark Desktops Imagine They Can Actually Compete With the Mac Studio
articles.content_orig:
New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC.
With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work.
Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops.
Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC.
As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks.
RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system.
Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks.
RTX Spark desktops are equipped with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128GB of unified memory, delivering up to 1 petaflop of AI performance. Ten-gigabit Ethernet connectivity enables fast transfers of large datasets, model files and creative assets between RTX Spark compact desktops and networked storage.
This advanced hardware unlocks incredible capabilities for creators, developers and AI enthusiasts, including:
New compact desktops are available for purchase from ASUS, Dell and MSI, joining the RTX Spark family of laptops available today. Mini PCs from Acer, GIGABYTE and HP are coming soon, along with the Microsoft Surface RTX Spark Dev Box .
Native CUDA support and Linux development tools through Windows Subsystem for Linux give developers a foundation for building and running local AI workflows. Developers can set up agents with Hermes Agent or NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and fine-tune supported models using Unsloth.
RTX Spark can run creative agents that connect familiar applications and local AI tools, helping creators move from an idea to finished work with natural-language instructions.
NVIDIA Switchyard, now available in Hermes, automatically routes agent tasks between local and cloud models. Everyday tasks can run on device, while advanced reasoning draws on cloud models, helping manage cloud costs across creative workflows.
These capabilities come together in creative workflows that connect Photoshop and ComfyUI through Hermes Agent. Using natural-language instructions, creators can turn sketches into rendered images and animations, or animate an image entirely on device — from isolating a subject and defining its motion to generating the finished video.
NVIDIA brought these workflows to life at Adobe MAX, where attendees used natural-language instructions to turn sketches into rendered images and animations for a shared digital Miami landscape.
The RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR features, already available in ComfyUI, extend the pipeline: a generated clip can be expanded to 60 frames per second and converted to high dynamic range for color grading, all within a single ComfyUI workflow on RTX Spark.
NVIDIA and Adobe are expanding native Windows on Arm support and RTX acceleration across Adobe’s creative applications, helping video editors, photographers, designers and 3D artists work more efficiently on RTX Spark.
Adobe Premiere accelerates a range of AI-powered editing features through NVIDIA TensorRT-RTX , including Enhance Speech, Object Mask, Scene Edit Detection and Auto Reframe — so editors spend less time waiting and more time cutting.
GPU acceleration also extends to Film Impact transition and effects plug-ins. The update improves support for professional video formats, including Canon RAW, Red RAW, ARRI RAW, ARRICORE, ARRI HDE, H.264 and HEVC in MXF, ProRes RAW and long-GOP video. This lets editors realize more than 50% quicker turnaround on everyday H.264 video deliverables.
Adobe Photoshop adds TensorRT-RTX acceleration for the Remove Tool and ArmRTX Spark-native Camera Raw support, helping photographers remove unwanted objects faster and work with RAW images without relying on emulation. At Adobe MAX, Adobe previewed a next-generation image processing engine with extensive GPU acceleration, including interactive Gaussian blur and Light Leaks filters.
Adobe Substance 3D Painter 12.2 is now optimized for RTX Spark with native support on Arm for the first time in public beta. Artists in games, visual effects and visualization can run Substance Painter natively on RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops, with no compatibility layer required.
Adobe Illustrator and InDesign now offer native Windows on Arm versions optimized for RTX Spark. Adobe Illustrator delivers up to 30% higher performance than its emulated version, helping accelerate illustration, graphic design and page-layout workflows on RTX Spark.
Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction into the Cycles viewport, helping artists evaluate lighting and materials with near-final-quality ray-traced previews as they work.
The practical difference is immediate: instead of navigating a noisy, resolving preview, Ray Reconstruction delivers near-final-quality lighting, reflections and materials in the interactive viewport in real time.
DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support requires Blender 5.3 and the latest NVIDIA Game Ready Driver or NVIDIA Studio Driver. Download the NVIDIA App to get automatic notifications when the latest drivers are available, optimize games and applications from a unified GPU control center, and discover the latest NVIDIA tools and software.
Announced at Microsoft Ignite, Windows Server is evolving for organizations that need to run AI closer to their enterprise applications and data.
Microsoft is expanding hardware choice through support for the latest AI silicon, helping customers take advantage of accelerated inference and increasingly capable models in their own environments. NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows platform powered by the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip is expanding to include support for Windows Server 2028.
New accelerator platforms and the breadth of the Windows silicon ecosystem provide customers options at different capability levels and price points for advanced AI development, local inference, and agent workloads at scale.
Also announced at Microsoft Ignite, developers can now bring any GGUF model from Hugging Face and run it within Windows ML using the llama.cpp backend.
The DxCGC backend, now available as an experimental release, is an integration for game developers that compiles and runs machine learning models through DirectX 12, allowing them to execute AI workloads alongside graphics.
Windows APIs let applications integrate platform-provided AI capabilities adding GPU support for AION Instruct and VSR.
Developers can also build high-performance AI models for Windows ML using the command line interface.
