articles.title_orig: Hospitals Rush to Patch Java Vulnerabilities
articles.title_zh: Hospitals Rush to Patch Java Vulnerabilities
articles.content_orig:
On November 17, 2026, the security research company Calif disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) , a memory-corruption vulnerability in the Base64 decoder of OpenJDK, the most widely used Java runtime. Under the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) 4.0, it scores 9.2 out of 10 (Critical). The flaw affects Java. OpenJDK published a security advisory and Oracle released patched builds in its November 2026 Critical Patch Update the same day, at 21:00 UTC.
The vulnerability lets a remote attacker with no credentials send malformed Base64 data to a Java application and overwrite memory next to the decoded output. Calif turned that overwrite into a leak of heap memory, similar to Heartbleed , and into remote code execution. Calif demonstrated pre-authentication remote code execution against Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate in their default configurations, and post-authentication remote code execution against Apache Kafka, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker.
Cloudflare has released a new set of rules in the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset designed to detect malformed Base64 input patterns associated with this vulnerability. The rules are available on Pro, Business and Enterprise plans and are enabled by default with the Log action because malformed input and some benign application-specific token formats can resemble exploitation attempts. Blocking by default could therefore disrupt legitimate traffic. Customers can review matching requests in Security Events now and change the rules action to Block once they confirm it does not affect legitimate traffic.Â
The WAF is an additional layer of defense, not a replacement for the patch. Java4Shell can be reached through paths a WAF does not see, like outbound TLS responses, and the only complete fix is to update the Java runtime. Our analysts continue to monitor attack activity and will update the rules as new techniques and variations appear. You can track rule changes in the WAF changelog and get more information on how the vulnerability develops on the dedicated Cloudflare Zero Wire briefing .
We have seen no indication so far that Java4Shell was exploited on Cloudflare infrastructure.
Base64 is a common way to represent binary data as text. Java applications decode Base64 when they process authentication headers, tokens, file uploads and many network messages. To decode it faster, OpenJDK replaces frequently used code with specialized machine code, called intrinsics. On supported x86-64 processors, the Base64 intrinsic uses AVX-512 instructions to process 64 bytes at a time.
The bug sits in the handwritten assembly that handles the final characters of the input. When the tail of the input contains padding characters (=) in a position where valid Base64 never places them, the routine calculates a negative output length. That invalid length turns into a full 64-byte write. For a 65-character input, made of 64 characters followed by a single =, OpenJDK allocates a 50-byte output array and then writes 62 bytes past its end.
Java eventually rejects the input as invalid and throws an exception. By then, the neighboring memory has already been overwritten. An application's own input validation does not help, because the corruption happens inside the decoder before the application can reject the data.
The simplest trigger is 64 A characters followed by =. On OpenJDK 17, the trigger needs 128 characters followed by =, because the threshold for the fast code path is higher.
Exploitation is not point-and-shoot. The overwritten bytes are mostly fixed values, and the attacker controls only where the write lands. To build a working exploit, Calif arranged the Java heap so that the overflow enlarged neighboring arrays, which gave them first a way to read heap memory and then a way to write chosen bytes. Each target application requires its own exploit chain. Calif reported developing its first working local exploit in about three hours with the help of AI agents, so we expect other attackers to build exploit chains quickly.
Java4Shell affects a system only when all the following conditions are true:
OpenJDK 17.0.6 or newer, including distributions built from OpenJDK: Amazon Corretto, Eclipse Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Azul Zulu, BellSoft Liberica, SAP SapMachine, Red Hat OpenJDK, Oracle OpenJDK, Oracle Java SE and Oracle GraalVM for JDK. Check Oracle's advisory for the exact list of affected Oracle builds.
x86-64 with AVX-512 VBMI support, such as Intel Xeon Ice Lake, Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids and Granite Rapids, or AMD EPYC and Ryzen Zen 4 or newer. ARM64 processors are not affected.
The application decodes attacker-controlled Base64 data with the standard Java decoder.
Many applications bundle their own Java runtime, and container images ship with a fixed Java Development Kit (JDK). Upgrading the system Java package does not update those copies, and it does not replace a Java virtual machine (JVM) that is already running. Every updated service needs a restart.
If you cannot update immediately, Calif documents two JVM startup flags that remove the vulnerable code path:
Both flags require a restart and may reduce performance for workloads that decode large amounts of Base64. They buy time while you patch. They do not replace the update.
Patching every Java runtime takes time, especially when JDKs are bundled inside applications and container images. Cloudflare WAF can reduce your exposure while you patch. A new managed rule, available on paid plans and enabled in Log mode by default, detects the malformed Base64 input that triggers Java4Shell. For Business and Enterprise customers, WAF attack score adds a machine learning layer that scores each request for remote code execution payloads, which helps catch variations and bypass attempts that signature-based rules can miss.
Protection for paid plans has been released as part of the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset (Ruleset ID efb7b8c949ac4650a09736fc376e9aee). The rule is enabled by default with the Log action, because blocking by default could cause false positives on legitimate Base64 traffic. To review its matches, go to Security > Security Analytics > Events and filter by the rule ID. If the matches are not legitimate traffic, change the rule action to Block: go to Security > Settings, edit the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset, search for CVE-2026-114938 and set the rule action to Block. Alternatively, you can follow the link to review your configuration on the Zero Wire briefing.

articles.title_orig: 14 Long Island hospitals get A grades in Leapfrog patient safety ranking, one gets D
articles.title_zh: 14 Long Island hospitals get A grades in Leapfrog patient safety ranking, one gets D
articles.content_orig:
Of the 23 Long Island hospitals ranked by The Leapfrog Group, a safety-focused nonprofit, 14 scored top marks for patient safety. Credit: Newsday
Fourteen Long Island hospitals scored top marks for patient safety in a national report published Wednesday.
Only three of the 23 Long Island hospitals ranked by The Leapfrog Group, a safety-focused nonprofit, received C grades in patient safety, based on how well they protected patients from accidents, infections and injuries. Only one Long Island hospital — Nassau University Medical Center — scored a D, down from a C in Leapfrog's fall 2025 ratings.
The Leapfrog Group’s rankings can help Long Islanders evaluate hospitals for some visits, but it’s important that prospective patients look at multiple reports — particularly recent reports — and consider costs and their health insurance, said Patricia Kelmar, senior director of healthcare campaigns for the consumer advocacy group PIRG, headquartered in Denver.
"You always want to see the most recent report and understand and know what that covers," Kelmar said. "Patient safety and quality has to be a daily priority for leadership in a hospital."
The Washington, D.C.-based Leapfrog evaluated 2,367 hospitals nationwide, with 900, or about 38%, receiving A grades, according to a news release from the nonprofit.

By clicking Sign up, you agree to our privacy policy .
"We want all our hospitals to get As," said Elisabeth Benjamin, vice president of health initiatives at the Manhattan-based Community Service Society of New York. "It means that the standard of care is improving."
Of the Long Island hospitals rated, seven A-grade hospitals were in Northwell Health’s network. Those hospitals are Glen Cove Hospital, Huntington Hospital, Mather Hospital in Port Jefferson, Plainview Hospital and Syosset Hospital.
North Shore University Hospital and South Shore University hospital — also Northwell Hospitals — both received A grades, up from B grades in Leapfrog’s spring 2026 report.
Chief quality officer for Northwell Health Peter Silver attributed the improvement at those two hospitals to lower infection rates, fewer complications from surgery and medications, and generally improved patient safety.
"We want to always be doing better and always be sure we’re providing the best care possible to our patients," Silver said. "I think these results reinforce that our strategy is working."
Three of Northwell’s hospitals, Long Island Jewish Medical Center, Long Island Jewish Valley Stream and Peconic Bay Medical Center in Riverhead, received B grades. Peconic Bay Medical center dropped in the ratings from an A grade in the spring.
Whether a hospital’s safety rating has improved or declined can help Long Islanders evaluate whether a hospital is investing in safety, Kelmar said.
"The history of the organization and the grades that they've had over time is a really important piece of the puzzle," Kelmar said. "Hospitals are run by human beings, and sometimes they're short on staff, there's a senior leadership change, or any number of things could cause a breakdown in their patient safety protocols."
Patients with doctors who can work out of multiple hospitals can also press their physician on what hospitals are safer, Kelmar added. Long Islanders can also examine the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services star ratings system and New York State’s hospital profiles , Benjamin added.
NYU Langone Hospital—Long Island and NYU Langone Hospital—Suffolk both maintained an A and B rating respectively from the spring.
Joseph Greco, executive vice president and chief of hospital operations for NYU Langone Hospital—Long Island in Mineola, said the health system has invested in NYU Langone Hospital—Suffolk since taking it over. NYU Langone completed its merger with Long Island Community Hospital, now NYU Langone Hospital—Suffolk, last year, Newsday reported.
"We’re seeing the progress that we have in all our hospitals take hold in Suffolk County," Greco said.
Mount Sinai South Nassau also received an A grade, the same as its spring score. The A grade comes after the hospital completed a $10 million expansion at the Oceanside hospital and opened five new operating rooms , Newsday reported.
"This has been a journey that we have taken very seriously," said Alan Wong, chief medical officer at Mount Sinai South Nassau. "This grade represents everyone at the hospital pulling together, working towards high quality care for our patients."
St. Joseph Hospital, a part of Catholic Health Long Island, received an A grade for Leapfrog’s fall 2026 report, up from a B in the spring 2026 report.
"Catholic Health is driven by a culture that places patient safety at the center of everything we do," Jason Golbin, executive vice president and chief medical officer at Catholic Health, said in a statement.
Also in Catholic Health’s network, Mercy Hospital in Rockville Centre, St. Catherine of Siena Hospital in Smithtown, St. Charles Hospital in Port Jefferson and St. Francis Hospital and Heart Center all received A grades, while Good Samaritan Hospital scored a C — the same as its spring 2026 score.
The Leapfrog Group gave two other hospitals on Long Island C grades: Stony Brook Eastern Long Island Hospital and Stony Brook University Hospital, which had scored a C in Leapfrog’s spring 2026 report. The Leapfrog Group did not grade Stony Brook Eastern Long Island Hospital in the spring.
Stony Brook Southampton hospital scored a B, up from a C in Leapfrog's spring 2026 report. Eric Morley, chief quality officer at Stony Brook Medicine, said in an emailed statement that the health system "constantly strive[s] for continuous improvement to achieve the best outcomes," and noted it had achieved high marks by other ranking systems.
Nassau University Medical Center was the only Long Island Hospital to receive a D rating, according to the Leapfrog Group.
NUMC serves a large number of patients on public insurance, and its debts reached $1.4 billion in 2025, Newsday reported.
NUMC leadership is working on a plan, due Dec. 1, to improve the facility’s finances, Newsday reported. Hospital leadership is considering building a new facility, rather than spending millions on repairs, Newsday reported.
Representatives for NUMC did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
A D grade is concerning, but Leah Binder, the president and CEO of the Leapfrog Group, encouraged prospective patients to do additional research and ask their physician about safety practices.
"If you see a hospital got a D, you can dig in and look at how they did on all 32 measures" that Leapfrog examines, Binder said. "Then you can ask some questions."

articles.title_orig: Leaker claims Apple developing four models of 20th anniversary iPhone
articles.title_zh: Leaker claims Apple developing four models of 20th anniversary iPhone
articles.content_orig:
Leaker Ice Universe says Apple is currently developing four models of the 20th anniversary iPhone which we’ve been referring to as the iPhone 20 . We’re expecting next year’s flagship models to be a radical new design with an all-glass appearance.
Why four models rather than two is unclear, but it seems possible Apple is testing two versions of both the Pro and the Pro Max to determine just how ambitious it can be with the final product …
Ice Universe says that two of the four models have quad-curved glass backs and two have flat glass. They indicate that Apple has already had to ramp back its ambitions with the curvature.
Apple is currently developing four models in total: two with flat glass backs and two with quad-curved glass backs. Apple has been prototyping this quad-curved design for three years, making several revisions along the way—particularly regarding the glass curvature, which is still being refined. The earliest version had a very pronounced curve; it was later reduced somewhat.
It’s standard practice for Apple to develop multiple competing prototypes of new devices, evaluating them for everything from usability and durability to ease of manufacturing.
We’re expecting Apple to use a combination of ultra-thin bezels and curved glass to create the illusion of no bezels at all – a more sophisticated version of the effect seen on the Apple Watch. Today’s report says the bezels are around 1mm thick.
The curved edges on the quad-curved version are approximately 1mm wide. However, because the glass curves around all sides, when viewed straight on from the front, the bezel becomes nearly invisible, creating a near‑borderless appearance. The actual visual effect could be quite stunning.
We yesterday saw an AI-generated render of what the design could look like. It’s expected to be the biggest redesign of the standard iPhone since the iPhone X.
FTC: We use income earning auto affiliate links. More.

articles.title_orig: The Philippines Serves Up Fried Chicken Diplomacy for Trump
articles.title_zh: The Philippines Serves Up Fried Chicken Diplomacy for Trump
articles.content_orig:
Move over, McDonald's — Jollibee is now on President Donald Trump's plate .
Filipino President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. gifted Trump and his delegation a late-night delivery of fried chicken from the beloved fast-food chain upon their arrival this week for the ASEAN Summit , bragging to the Americans that the menu item has now surpassed Kentucky Fried Chicken in the good ol' US of A.
"Since you're strapped for time, I thought the taste of Manila might be good," Marcos told Trump in a video released by state television in the Philippines.
"So last night I asked my staff to have some Jollibee delivered as a late-night snack for you and your delegation. I think they gave you the– Jollibee is a very popular chain. And one of their main products is fried chicken. And we are very proud to say that we have surpassed KFC in the United States in terms of popularity."
"Oh, wow," Trump said. "Fantastic."
"So we thought that would give you a taste of of of Manila. And I think I hope some of your staff was also able to partake. You have been working very hard, Mr. President, so just think of it as providing extra energy for all the work that you have to do, that you've done and continue to do and that is in front of you."
It's not the first time an international leader has used fast food to appeal to the current American president.
In May 2025, the Saudis brought a McDonald's in a truck for Trump during his trip to the Middle East.
Trump's affection for the American stalwart of fast food, McDonald's, is well documented.
While running for his second White House term, Trump put on an apron and served drive-thru customers of the Double Arches in Pennsylvania during a campaign stop
During Trump's first term in 2019, Trump had a table laid out in the White House full of Big Macs, nuggets, fries and other goodies for the Clemson Tigers football team when the athletes from South Carolina's Clemson University visited after winning the National Championship a year earlier.

articles.title_orig: Here’s how much Medicare Part B premiums are rising in 2027
articles.title_zh: Here’s how much Medicare Part B premiums are rising in 2027
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Medicare, which provides health insurance coverage to roughly 75 million retired seniors and disabled workers in the US, is getting more expensive next year.
Medicare Part B premiums, which cover doctors, outpatient care, some home healthcare services, and durable medical equipment, will rise about 3.2% to $209.40 a month in 2027, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) announced Tuesday .
That's an increase of $6.50 a month from $202.90 in 2026, bringing the total premium to $2,512.80 a year.
The Medicare Part B premium is deducted from your Social Security checks before you receive them. The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027 . Starting in January, the increase will add an average of $75 per month.
That is great news, but the Medicare premium increase will eat into it.
The annual deductible for all Medicare Part B beneficiaries increases to $292 in 2027, up $9 from $283 in 2026.
The increase in the standard premium and deductible is mainly due to projected increases in healthcare spending, according to CMS.
Read more: How to add or adjust your Medicare coverage
People with traditional Medicare generally pay the Part B premium for physician coverage and a separate one for prescription drug coverage, known as Part D. Those premiums vary by plan. Some people pay an additional monthly premium for inpatient hospital coverage (Part A).
Each year, the Medicare Part B premium, deductible, and coinsurance rates are reset. If you're enrolled in traditional Medicare, you also have a Part D drug plan. The 2027 Part D base premium is $36 per month on average, but yours could be higher.
"Americans clearly understand that healthcare costs can threaten their retirement security," Kelly LaVigne, vice president of Consumer Insights at Allianz Life, told Yahoo Finance. But "so many don't fully understand what Medicare will and won't cover. And the details matter."
Roughly 15% of the average retiree's annual expenses will be health-related, according to Fidelity. On average, a 65-year-old who leaves the workforce this year may need $185,500 in savings to cover out-of-pocket healthcare expenses throughout retirement.
Even though the program offers fairly comprehensive coverage, traditional Medicare does not have an annual out-of-pocket limit.
The biggest hardship for many people enrolled in original Medicare is that Part B pays only 80% of expenses.
To cover the rest, you need to purchase a Medigap health insurance policy, sold by private insurers, that covers the remaining expenses.
For Medicare and Medicare Advantage users looking to make changes to their plans, the open enrollment period for 2027 ends Dec. 7.
Kerry Hannon is a Senior Columnist at Yahoo Finance. She is a career and retirement strategist and the author of 14 books, including " Retirement Bites: A Gen X Guide to Securing Your Financial Future, " " In Control at 50+: How to Succeed in the New World of Work ," and "Never Too Old to Get Rich.

articles.title_orig: Ethiopia and Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears, sources say
articles.title_zh: Ethiopia and Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears, sources say
articles.content_orig:
After a few weeks of relative stability , fresh clashes in the contested Ethiopia-Eritrea border area have raised fears of a full-fledged war. Meanwhile, diplomatic relations between Ethiopia and Sudan have hit new lows.
Fighters allied with the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) launched their offensive on September 23 . It was aimed at overthrowing the Ethiopian government as part of a larger rebel coalition. But the Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF), backed by pro-government militia, have steadily pushed the TPLF out of Tigray, a region in northern Ethiopia .
According to the conflict tracker of the monitoring organization ACLED, the ENDF have pushed further into Tigray, effectively driving the Tigrayan Defense Forces (TDF) towards the border with Eritrea. Skirmishes have been reported from several locations, while the ENDF have fired heavy artillery towards dwellings close to the Eritrean border town of Badme.
While no census data is publicly available, Badme appears to be a small rural town on satellite images. However, the locality is historically significant for both sides because it was the ground zero of the Eritrean-Ethiopian War from 1998 to 2000, sometimes dubbed the Badme War.
The war ended with the Algiers Agreement , in which both countries agreed to honor the rulings of a newly formed Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission. The commission awarded Badme to Eritrea , a decision that Ethiopia challenged at times. Abdurahman Sayed, director of the London-based Horn of Africa Center for Regional Integration, told DW that Ethiopia might see an advantage in reclaiming Badme to resolve its current internal struggles.
"It seems now if the Eritreans withdrew and the Ethiopians came back, it could be to calm down the Tigrayans, especially those who are now supporting the party in power in Ethiopia", Sayed said.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
He suggested that people like Getachew Reda, a former spokesman for the TPLF and current advisor to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, might be able to win the Tigrayan people over to side with the federal government through territorial gains for the Tigray region.
"The coming of the forces to the Eritrean-Ethiopian border clearly indicates that the conflict can be triggered any time ", Abdurahman Sayed said.
Eritrean and Ethiopian government troops allied against the Tigrayan forces during the 2020-22 Tigray conflict. Since then, Eritrea's allegiances have shifted towards the TPLF and away from Abiy Ahmed's central government. In October, the two neighbors cut diplomatic ties . At one point, Eritrean troops reportedly crossed the border into Tigray .
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Magnus Taylor, a regional analyst with the International Crisis Group (ICG), believes that Addis Ababa's prime objective for the moment might rather be securing its northern border and destroying supply lines between Eritrea and Tigrayan forces.
"So what we might actually be seeing is a kind of a function of the attempts by the Ethiopian military to consolidate its control of Tigray, which includes pushing Tigray's borders with Eritrea", Taylor told DW.
However, securing control over Tigray could also involve direct conflict with Eritrea at one point, Taylor said: "If this happens, then it's quite likely that the Ethiopians would attempt to carry out all their objectives in Eritrea at one time."
Since Eritrea seceded from Ethiopia in 1993, Ethiopia has been the world's largest landlocked country by population. Prime Minister Abiy has repeatedly described the country's lack of sea access as an existential threat. While stating a preference for peaceful means to gain access, he said this could also mean capturing Eritrea's easternmost port, Assab , by force.
At the same time, the diplomatic relations between Ethiopia and its northwestern neighbor, Sudan, have deteriorated even further.
Sudan and Egypt , both downstream the river Nile, have been on edge for years because of Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance Dam (GERD) . The massive GERD, built on the Blue Nile just kilometers from Ethiopia's border with Sudan, gives Addis Ababa significant leverage over the timing and regulation of water flows downstream, raising concerns in Sudan and Egypt over water security and dam operations. The Ethiopian government has rejected claims that the dam could be used as a means to pressure Sudan and Egypt .
Since 2023, Sudan has been embroiled in a civil war between two rival military forces: the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), led by General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF ) , led by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti . In mid-November, both sides accused the other of direct participation in each other's internal conflicts.
Two countries with severe internal conflicts and mirroring alliances: Could the situation deteriorate further into potential direct fights between the two armies? ICG's Magnus Taylor believes there is a risk, but at least not for now.
"The most likely scenario is we just get a continuation of this kind of proxy style of involvement with each other's opposition groups rather than formal direct involvement on the ground in the conflict," Taylor said.
Sayed also believes that, at the moment, there is no need for direct confrontation.
"The RSF can do the job that Ethiopia and any other country backing them wants them to do," Sayed said. "But if there is a need and the RSF are failing, the Ethiopian army could be pushed to get involved."

articles.title_orig: 3,300-year-old bronze sword emerges from Italian lake and still has a 'sharp edge'
articles.title_zh: 3,300-year-old bronze sword emerges from Italian lake and still has a 'sharp edge'
articles.content_orig:
Underwater archaeologists have recovered an exceptionally well-preserved Early Bronze Age sword from an ancient settlement beneath an Italian volcanic lake. The 3,300-year-old weapon is reportedly still sharp, offering a glimpse into the lives and possible rituals of the people who once inhabited the site.
The 13th-century BC discovery occurred in the final stages of an underwater archaeological expedition at Lake Mezzano in Italy’s central Lazio region, and has been announced by Italy’s Superintendency of Archaeology, Fine Arts & Landscape for the Province of Viterbo and Southern Etruria, a department of the Ministry of Culture .
The authority’s Underwater Archaeology Service was working alongside the Rome Carabinieri Underwater Unit when the weapon was discovered off the lake’s southern shore, an area previously relatively uninvestigated.
The Carabinieri divers supported the archaeological divers with underwater surveying, documentation and operational safety.
Specialist underwater conservators from CSR Restauro Beni Culturali assisted with the delicate recovery process, enabling conservation measures to begin immediately after the artefacts were brought to the surface.
The sword is the third to be recovered from Lake Mezzano since archaeological investigations began in the 1970s.
The lake was formed in the crater of an ancient volcano about 100km north-west of Rome. The substantial prehistoric settlement beneath its surface contains dwellings that would originally have been supported above water level by wooden piles.
The latest excavation has also produced intact ceramic vessels and numerous other bronze objects, including axes, arrowheads, daggers, spearheads, pins and a razor, all found at consistent depths in different parts of the site.
The sword was found near the razor, and similar combinations documented at other Bronze Age archaeological sites are thought possibly to indicate a connection with individuals of elevated social standing, such as members of a warrior elite.
Bronze Age communities are thought to have sometimes deliberately deposited weapons including swords, axes and spearheads along with other objects in water as part of ritual or religious practices.
The archaeological authority says that investigations will continue over the coming years, using underwater stratigraphic excavation and advanced recording and spatial-mapping techniques. A selection of the recovered bronze objects is also expected to feature in a forthcoming exhibition.

articles.title_orig: 'PS5 Pro Is Not Powerful Enough to Run GTA 6 at 60fps': Rockstar Explains Frame Rate Decision
articles.title_zh: 'PS5 Pro Is Not Powerful Enough to Run GTA 6 at 60fps': Rockstar Explains Frame Rate Decision
articles.content_orig:
I’ve played GTA 6 on PS5 Pro for over 150 hours and it’s a remarkable experience. You can read my review through here .
This is the densest open world ever designed. The sheer amount of art assets on screen at any given time is simply unprecedented.
There is a downside to all the detail, though: the Rockstar release bucks contemporary console trends and runs at 30fps, without compromise. There’s no Performance option, even on Sony’s most powerful platform, which will run you $900 these days.
I spoke to Rockstar’s Marc Chambers, the man in charge of Technology Production to try to understand why.
“The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the games visual fidelity,” he said.
“While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it’s not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”
In other words, it’s as many already predicted: GTA 6’s performance is limited by its robust CPU demands.
Chambers continued: “GTA 6 pushes the current-generation console hardware to its absolute limits. The complexity of simulating and rendering the environments and inhabitants in a world the scale of Leonida, while maintaining the density, visual fidelity, and player agency we envisaged, places extraordinary demands on the hardware. Bringing all of these systems together and completing the required work for every frame is only just possible within a ~33ms frame budget.”
The remarkable thing to me is, despite the drop to 30fps, I found the game to feel very responsive overall. Aiming is snappy and movement feels less cumbersome than in past Rockstar releases, like Red Dead Redemption 2 .
Rockstar’s Vice President of Technology David Hynd told me that the team was able to remove one full frame of delay compared to past titles.
“The input controller is sampled as late as possible during the game update. As a consequence, the game is updated with the most recent input data and we minimise the time between pressing a button and seeing the results on screen,” he said.
You really do feel this: I was switching between GTA 6 and several other 60fps PS5 games during the review process, and while the frame rate difference was obvious to my eyes, it didn’t feel as dramatic as I’d expected.
“For our game mechanics, we ensured that we stripped as much ‘dead space’ out of the start of our animations as possible,” Hynd continued. “And ensured that we could seamlessly interrupt them as early as was practical.”
There are still moments where GTA 6 feels clumsy, but it’s a marked improvement in playability compared to past games, despite the drop in frame rate.
Overall, I think Rockstar made the right decision.
The decision to lock gameplay at 30fps is objectively disappointing, but on a PS5 Pro the performance is smooth throughout, and the controller response is surprisingly good.
With the sheer amount of art assets on the screen at any given time, I think it would have been a shame to see Rockstar compromise its vision.
This is the most immersive open world ever made, and I think it’s clear the team has put as much thought as possible into making sure it feels smooth and responsive at 30fps.

articles.title_orig: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X
articles.title_zh: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X
articles.content_orig:
Copies of GTA 6 are beginning to arrive, with one difference spotted between the Xbox and PlayStation versions.
Grand Theft Auto VI ’s November 19 launch is almost finally upon us, with copies of the game already in the hands of many.
Preloads for digital copies of the game began on November 10 after Rockstar Games shifted the date forwards due to the title’s enormous file size .
For those who opted for code-in-a-box copies, preloads open today, on November 12.
Those who have a code-in-a-box copy in hand have taken to social media to reveal that the box features a double-sided fold-up poster, which is a nice touch.
One side features Lucia, with GTA VI ’s key art appearing on the other; the Grand Theft Auto franchise’s classic art style is used.
What has now been realised, however, is that those with an Xbox code-in-a-box copy are getting a slight downgrade compared to their PlayStation counterparts.
X (formerly Twitter) user GameRiot took to the site to share that “the GTA VI poster is actually smaller on Xbox compared to PS5”.
You can see in the video clip below that we’re not talking a couple of milimetres here.
There is likely a very good reason for this, as GameRiot points out, and that’s all down to case sizing.
While PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S physical cases are similarly sized, it appears that the area for posters, booklets, and such like within the Xbox case is slightly smaller.
Therefore, GTA VI ’s poster has been made smaller to fit accordingly, rather than this being any form of intentional slight to Xbox users.
It may feel that way amid Rockstar Games and PlayStation’s ongoing “plays best” marketing campaign that favours Sony’s console.
What isn’t abundantly clear yet is whether this difference in poster sizing is worldwide or whether this is unique to where GameRiot is based in the UK.
Grand Theft Auto fans are definitely seeing the humour in this latest spot.
“Cancelled my pre-order, unplayable,” joked BanksniO.
“They taking plays best on PS5 too seriously,” added vce_bby.
It’s a shame that Jason doesn’t get the chance to shine on the poster, unless he’s going to pop up elsewhere.
GameRiot did confirm that the PS5’s poster is roughly A3 sized while Xbox’s is understandably somewhat below A3 which could make the Xbox version difficult to frame, if that’s something you’re interested in.
READ MORE: GTA 6's first player ratings surface early via PlayStation Store, oops
It’s definitely been a busy week for GTA VI with an endless stream of marketing continuing to rollout.
Rockstar Games announced GTA VI : The Festival , a once-in-a-lifetime launch party based in Miami, Florida, plus Metacritic and Fandom have revealed a contest where you could win up to $500 in Visa gift cards simply by predicting GTA VI ’s Metacritic score .
We’ve also had confirmation that GTA VI will only run at 30fps , including on the PlayStation 5 Pro - something that’s ruffled a few feathers.
If you haven’t preloaded your game already, you may want to this weekend. GTA VI will be here before you know it.

articles.title_orig: Waymo suspends all driverless taxi rides on freeways after ban in California
articles.title_zh: Waymo suspends all driverless taxi rides on freeways after ban in California
articles.content_orig:
Waymo has temporarily stopped offering driverless taxi rides on freeways after California banned the vehicles from state freeways following recent traffic incidents.
The company had allowed riders to hail its robotaxis for freeway rides in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin. The California-based company offers rides on city streets in many other areas including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver.
A Waymo spokesperson wrote in an email that the company has “temporarily restricted commercial freeway rides in all markets where we operate that service,” though it’s “continuing freeway testing with trained autonomous specialists behind the wheel.” The suspension was implemented last Wednesday, according to the spokesperson, but they didn't say how long it would last.
Related video: Why are gas prices dropping and how low will they go?
The suspension came after the California Department of Motor Vehicles banned the company's robotaxis from freeways that same day. The ban followed two incidents including one in which three Waymo driverless vehicles drove into a construction zone, DMV spokesperson Jonathan Groveman said in a statement.
The construction zone incident occurred on Nov. 5 and the second incident, which involved California Highway Patrol vehicles, occurred the next day on a highway in San Francisco, according to Groveman.
Video of the Nov. 6 incident circulated widely on social media last week. In the footage, a Waymo vehicle can be seen trying to bypass California Highway Patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break.
“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” Groveman said.
Groveman added that “similar incidents” previously occurred on May 18.
The Waymo spokesperson said the “recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California” did not “involve any injuries or collisions.”
California's restrictions bar Waymo from operating and testing its driverless vehicles on California freeways, according to Groveman. He said the restrictions will remain in effect until “Waymo demonstrates to the Department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions.”
Kelety reported from Phoenix.

articles.title_orig: Almost nobody’s vying for an invite to Trump’s second meme coin dinner
articles.title_zh: Almost nobody’s vying for an invite to Trump’s second meme coin dinner
articles.content_orig:
A mysterious digital finance firm with a CEO who goes by one name and plans to build a "Chinese $TRUMP coin community" appears to have rocketed into the top spot in the competition to attend President Trump's upcoming cryptocurrency gala dinner.
The firm FastX, which has ties to Singapore, claims to have amassed more than $2 million in $TRUMP coin in the past two months. The CEO of its parent company, who goes by Addy, is now boasting on social media about the potential to rub elbows with the American president.
"We are the number one Trump holder now. We have over 2 million tokens," a woman identified as Addy said in a video posted to X on Nov. 11. "So later this month our team will attend a VIP reception with President Trump. So it's a big moment for us and the FastX community."
The opaque nature of the event, in which those competing for access to the presidential gala do so by acquiring large quantities of the Trump-branded meme coin, has renewed questions about the potential for corruption as the president's family venture does business with investors from across the globe .
The event on Sunday, Nov. 22, will be held at the Trump National Golf Club outside Washington, D.C., and will seat the 185 largest holders of the $TRUMP coin — a novelty product whose value rises and falls with the interest of buyers.
The website of the Trump company that sells the digital coins, Fight Fight Fight LLC, displays a public leaderboard for the event. The list identifies the top 130 holders only by usernames and crypto wallets, but does not disclose who is behind them.
On its website marketing the dinner, the company says, "No attendees will be granted a private meet & greet with the President," but Mr. Trump is advertised as the featured speaker at the event.
Little is known about FastX or Addy. The company, a subsidiary of something called GA Ventures Ltd., appears to be less than one year old . Early in October, FastX threw a yacht party during the TOKEN2049 crypto conference in Singapore. Eric Trump spoke at the conference, where he promoted the growth of crypto during his father's presidency.
"America is doing so great right now," Eric Trump said on stage during the crypto event at the Marina Bay Sands. "The way it's embraced cryptocurrency under my father's administration has been amazing."
Just a few weeks after the Singapore conference, FastX landed on the $TRUMP coin leaderboard. FastX's main wallet now holds nearly 1.8 million $TRUMP tokens, about 66% more than the next closest holder.
The company boasted about it in another video posted on X, which appears to have been filmed in an office in Centennial Tower in the Marina Bay area of Singapore. CBS News determined the location based on the facades of buildings appearing in the background and an address previously listed in an archived version of the FastX website.
"We hold Trump coins because we believe in it," Addy said in the video.
CEO of GA Ventures, $TRUMP on FastX. The $TRUMP Hour. What it all means for FastX traders. Everything you need to know. Watch below. https://t.co/tj4dLdUEIO 🔥 pic.twitter.com/nJBqLl5Iak
This comes as congressional Democrats, newly emboldened by sweeping midterm election victories, say they are preparing investigations into the president's crypto businesses.
Mr. Trump has earned more than $1 billion from his crypto ventures during his second term, according to financial disclosures, including at least $635 million in royalties last year from a licensing deal tied to the meme coin.
"Foreign nationals and bad actors are apparently only too happy to seek access and favors by buying into Trump's meme coin scheme," said Sen. Richard Blumenthal, a Democrat from Connecticut, in a statement to CBS News. "He has put a 'For Sale' sign on the White House through the  $TRUMP coin and other crypto dealings." Blumenthal is set to chair the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations when Democrats take control of the Senate in January.
Earlier this month, Mr. Trump addressed his crypto profits during an interview with "60 Minutes," saying he has left those ventures in the hands of his sons, who oversee the Trump Organization.
"I have a company. My sons run the company," he said. "It's hard to say to them, 'Don't do anything anymore for four years because I'm president.'"
Regardless of the scrutiny, planning for the gala is forging ahead. Last week, Fight Fight Fight — the meme coin's parent company tied to the Trump family — announced that four "legends" will be joining the president for the event: Professional boxer Floyd Mayweather, "Shark Tank" star Kevin O'Leary, NBA champion Tristan Thompson and mentalist Lior Surchard. VIP attendees of the dinner are told to expect commemorative items including a Trump-branded watch and Trump-branded fragrance.
FastX representatives plan to attend the gala this weekend in Virginia, according to the video.
"It's a chance to meet the people who also support the Trump coin community," Addy said.
FastX also encourages users to join the company's "Chinese $TRUMP coin community," which is a curated feed of information about the meme coin, hosted by the cryptocurrency company Binance. Binance , whose CEO Chenpeng Zhao was pardoned by Mr. Trump in 2025, bars U.S.-based users from its platform. CBS News was automatically blocked from signing up on a U.S.-based computer.
FastX and GA Ventures did not respond to CBS News' request for comment.
Last month, CBS News reported that more than half of the crypto wallets on the Trump gala leaderboard at the time had used Binance or other crypto exchanges that prohibit U.S. users, suggesting many of the users were foreign-based.
At the time the gala contest closed Monday morning, 79 of the top 130 wallets had used a crypto exchange that bars U.S. users. Together, they hold about $8.8 million of the board's $9.5 million worth of $TRUMP coin.
FastX has touted its prospective access to the U.S. president, offering followers the chance to submit questions that FastX claims it will pose to the president at the gala dinner.
In posts on X last month, FastX said, "Got a question for Trump? Comment it below," and said it "will put 10 randomly selected questions forward at the upcoming dinner." FastX later added the disclaimer, "Questions are not guaranteed to be asked."
Followers responded with questions focused on the U.S. war with Iran, the increase in prices of goods, and concerns about the stability of the crypto markets.
"Mr. President, you called yourself the first Crypto President," one X user wrote. "What's the one crypto law you want to get signed before this dinner ends?"
"Clearly this FastX $TRUMP coin promotion is a way to get their company a direct audience with the president," said Corey Frayer, the director of investor protection for the Consumer Federation of America.
"It's incredibly corrosive to people's faith in our democracy when the highest ranking official and most powerful person in the world is selling away government decisions to line his pockets, not to do what's best for Americans."
Neither the White House nor Fight Fight Fight responded to requests for comment.
Since the midterm elections earlier this month, crypto products tied to the Trump family have been trading at an all-time low. The price of $TRUMP coin fell to around 92 cents this week, down significantly from its 2025 high of $74 a coin.

articles.title_orig: Fed’s Waller says central bank may need to ‘shock people’ with half-point rate hike
articles.title_zh: Fed’s Waller says central bank may need to ‘shock people’ with half-point rate hike
articles.content_orig:
Fed Governor Waller is becoming increasingly concerned about the US inflation outlook, warning that price pressures are broadening beyond energy and that the Fed risks allowing higher inflation to become entrenched in consumers' and businesses' expectations.
Waller argues that the central bank needs to take a more aggressive action to convince markets and the public that it remains committed to bringing inflation back to its 2% target.
He highlighted that roughly 70% of components in the core services basket are currently experiencing inflation above 3%, suggesting that price pressures are no longer concentrated in energy-related categories.
He is concerned that businesses are becoming comfortable passing higher prices on to consumers, partly because they believe consumers remain resilient enough to absorb those increases.
If businesses expect to raise prices and consumers increasingly accept 3% inflation as normal, inflation expectations could become more entrenched, making it harder for the Fed to bring inflation back down, without a more aggressive tightening.
He thinks the Fed needs to break the psychology that inflation around 3% has become the new norm after failing to bring it back to the 2% target since 2021. He stressed that the Fed needs to become more aggressive, either by delivering a 50 bps rate hike or use monetary policy communications to signal a significantly tougher stance in the months ahead.
Simply maintaining the current policy trajectory might not be enough to change inflation expectations. The Fed needs to convince businesses, consumers and financial markets that it is prepared to take stronger action to restore price stability. He even suggested that the central bank might need to go beyond reversing the rate cuts implemented last year to bring inflation under control.
He also argued that the Fed should use  statements, press conferences and forward guidance to steer market expectations towards a more restrictive policy outlook. A hawkish communication strategy could push  interest rate expectations higher and tightening financial conditions enough to weigh on economic activity and inflation.
He also questioned the usefulness of the December Summary of Economic Projections (SEP), arguing that year-end projections might not adequately capture the evolving inflation picture. He prefers adopting a more forceful and forward-looking communication strategy rather than relying too heavily on projections that could quickly become outdated.
For now, Waller remains the only governor suggesting a more aggressive action, with the majority of Fed members preferring to move in small steps. Nevertheless, he's been a very influential member and his views have always preceded a change in monetary policy since 2021.
In the current context, traders should be very careful buying risk assets unless the Iran war ends or the Fed turns surprisingly dovish.

articles.title_orig: 2028 Ford Mustang GTD Gets A Special Edition 125 Years In The Making
articles.title_zh: 2028 Ford Mustang GTD Gets A Special Edition 125 Years In The Making
articles.content_orig:
The Ford Mustang GTD has been updated for the 2028 model year. Besides minor changes, Ford has introduced a new special edition honoring “Sweepstakes”—the car Henry Ford built and raced in 1901.
The 2028 Ford Mustang GTD 1901 edition is painted in a shade called Royal Red paired with a black livery, gloss black wheels with red brake calipers and a carbon fibre splitter, diffuser, rocker panels and rear spoiler. It also gets the Performance Package as standard.
The interior of the 1901 special edition has a two-tone color scheme, featuring Mahogany Red leather seats with Race Red stitching, black door pads with Mahogany Red accents and a black dashboard.
Besides the special edition, the 2028 Mustang GTD comes with 3D-printed titanium paddle shifters, leather-wrapped centre console, and leather around the instrument binnacle. Customers also get the option of magnesium wheels. Ford has also updated the livery options for the standard Mustang GTD.
Ford’s flagship Mustang remains unchanged under the skin. It is powered by the same 5.2-liter V8 engine that delivers 815 hp and 664 lb-ft of torque to the rear axle via an 8-speed dual-clutch transaxle.
Bookings for the 2028 Mustang GTD will commence in December, with deliveries expected to begin in Q2 of 2027.

articles.title_orig: Xi, Putin Assail Trade Barriers Ahead of Summit With Trump
articles.title_zh: Xi, Putin Assail Trade Barriers Ahead of Summit With Trump
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By Liz Lee, Laurie Chen and Jarrett Renshaw
SHENZHEN, China, Nov 18 (Reuters) - China's President Xi Jinping on Wednesday pledged to stand up against trade protectionism, but also gave a warm welcome to US President Donald Trump as he arrived ahead of a high-stakes trilateral meeting that will include the Russian leader Vladimir Putin.
Xi greeted Trump at the airport, the first time he had ‌done so with any visiting leader since becoming president, reciprocating his counterpart's gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September when they last met.
Trump's arrival came after Xi and Putin delivered pointed speeches ahead of ‌an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen.
In his opening address, Xi urged support for what he called "free and open trade," trying to portray his country as a stable partner on the global stage, in contrast with the US, which has raised ​tariffs and taken a volatile approach to foreign policy under Trump.
In his speech, Putin criticised Western sanctions imposed over Russia's war in Ukraine.
At the Shenzhen airport, Xi and Trump briefly hugged and exchanged words before walking to their motorcades.
"China is a country of etiquette and has a tradition of reciprocating courtesy," Xi was quoted as saying by state news agency Xinhua. He added he was looking forward to discussing China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation and the global landscape.
Trump said every meeting with Xi has been "very pleasant," Xinhua reported.
They then joined Putin and other leaders at the APEC summit venue for handshakes, a group photo and banquet.
The three men will meet on the sidelines on Thursday and potentially discuss Russia's war with Ukraine and ‌the US war in Iran, as well as other flashpoints such as trade, ⁠ AI and nuclear weapons.
The meeting has drawn comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference between the US, Britain and the Soviet Union that formalised spheres of influence, set the stage for the post-World War Two order and became shorthand for great-power deals imposed on smaller countries.
It has also unnerved some European and Asian capitals, which fear the world's greatest military powers will ⁠disregard their interests.
MESSAGE RESONATES WITH GLOBAL SOUTH
Xi's remarks came after Washington announced further restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia, which could further complicate a fragile trade truce with Beijing. China has pledged to retaliate.
"We must firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, support free and open trade and investment," Xi told an audience of business executives.
Western trade partners have criticised China for running annual trade surpluses exceeding $1 trillion through policies that support ​its ​manufacturing sector at the expense of its consumers.
Beijing says its growth model is appropriate for an economy still catching up with the ​world's richest, but Washington, Brussels and others are concerned about China's supply chain dominance ‌providing the country with geopolitical leverage and say its policies threaten their industries and jobs.
Xi said China will continue to invest in its industrial complex and new technologies. The world's second-largest economy will lower tariffs and further open up its markets, while standing up against protectionism and unilateralism, he added.
His "message is likely to resonate with many Global South countries and reinforces Beijing's effort to contrast its technology strategy with that of Washington," said George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group.
Trump's trip to Asia is his first since his Republican Party's defeat in midterm elections this month, while allegations involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy add to the tension.
COLD RECEPTION FOR TAKAICHI
Leaders from Australia, Canada, South Korea and others were met by dancers and soldiers hoisting rifles, but Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi landed without any welcoming ceremony.
Her visit to China comes amid a rift between Beijing and Tokyo that ‌began a year ago after she said Japan could deploy its military if a Chinese move on Taiwan also threatened its territory.
On ​Tuesday, Taiwan and Japan flagged incursions by Russian aircraft into their airspace.
Putin, who was speaking after Ukraine crippled the vital Kerch road bridge ​linking Crimea to Russia in a major blow to his four-year-old war, followed Xi on stage with a ​speech that described Western powers as "former hegemons."
He said Europe was in a "humiliating decline" and anti-Russian sanctions imposed after his invasion of Ukraine had backfired.
"Experience has shown that the traditional tools ‌of economic dominance and de facto coercion have largely run their course, having lost ​much of their intimidating power," Putin said.
"While sanctions, tariffs, and ​export restrictions may still exert a certain deterrent effect, they are incapable of halting growth—let alone crushing the economies of competitors."
In Manila, Trump vowed to deepen defence cooperation with the Philippines, amid its growing friction with Beijing over disputed features in the South China Sea. Earlier, he floated the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China, but that has not been confirmed.
The Kremlin this week dismissed comparisons ​with the Yalta Conference as "games of political scientists," but said the meeting will have ‌a major impact on global affairs. Beijing said the trilateral will promote world peace.
Putin described the world as "turbulent" but said disagreements can be addressed by "sitting at the table."
"I therefore expect big potential ​benefit from the upcoming trilateral meeting," he said.
(Reporting by Liz Lee, Laurie Chen, Trevor Hunnicutt and Ju-Min Park in Shenzhen, Jekaterīna Golubkova in Tokyo, Farah Master in Hong Kong, and Shi Bu ​in Beijing; Writing by Marius Zaharia; editing by David Brunnstrom, Christian Schmollinger, Kate Mayberry, Saad Sayeed and Chizu Nomiyama )

articles.title_orig: In Choosing Shenzhen for Trump-Putin Summit, Xi Shows Off His Tech Ambitions
articles.title_zh: In Choosing Shenzhen for Trump-Putin Summit, Xi Shows Off His Tech Ambitions
articles.content_orig:
Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy
I n a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping , is basking in its neon glow.
On the sidelines, a series of high-profile bilateral meetings and the announcement of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have cemented Xi’s status as an agenda setter on the global stage.
The broader Apec summit , meanwhile, provides an opportunity for China to present itself as a steward of multilateralism against what it terms “unilateralism and protectionism” – that is to say, trade measures taken against Beijing by countries such as the US.
All this is set against the futuristic backdrop that is Shenzhen, a city that perhaps better than no other embodies China’s rise into a confident, technologically innovative power central to the global economy.
A photo display in the Apec media centre charts Shenzhen’s transformation from sparsely populated marshland, calling it “a miracle in the history of world development created by the Chinese people”.
“[Xi] wants people to go home Chinamaxxing,” said Prof Astrid Nordin, of King’s College London. “Shenzhen is itself part of the message. It’s a showcase of Chinese technological and economic achievements, and of China’s claim that it offers opportunities for prosperity in a world increasingly characterised by uncertainty and conflict.”
Like the light show, the summit is being carefully coordinated. The Financial Times cited people familiar with the matter as saying it would be one of the most tightly controlled in the organisation’s history, with leaders having to travel to a state guesthouse beside Shenzhen’s tiger safari park to meet Xi. The paper said diplomats had grumbled that the format “seems designed to reduce the free-flowing discussion characteristic of prior editions”.
Setting out its expectations for the summit, China’s foreign ministry has said it looks forward to “practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, AI and so on”.
Already, Xi has announced trade wins with Canada’s Mark Carney, extending remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products by two years in exchange for tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.
A meeting with Papua New ⁠Guinea’s leader, meanwhile, showed how Beijing’s geopolitical priorities have been absorbed and reflected by its allies, with James Marape recounting to Xi how he had closed Taiwan’s office in his country despite domestic challenges in doing so.
The most important meeting will be between Xi and Trump. The leaders of the world’s two superpowers are expected to tackle a broad range of issues including AI and trade. In a move that could strain the fragile tariff truce that the two leaders first agreed last year, the Trump administration said on Monday it would further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips.
Christopher Adams, a senior adviser at the law firm Covington who was at the centre of trade negotiations with China for the Obama and first Trump administrations, said: “The trade truce may increasingly look like a ceasefire in a war where major combat operations remain on hold but skirmishes are escalating to the point where the line between peace and war is blurred.
“I don’t see pressure to announce a further extension of the trade truce in Shenzhen. If a significant extension is announced, that would be an upside surprise.”
China has not hesitated to leverage Apec’s multinational platform in service of its arguments. A commentary by the state news agency Xinhua on Tuesday said: “Amid deepening geopolitical rivalries and growing global divisions, [China’s hosting] sends a clear signal that great-power competition need not be a zero-sum game, and that one country’s development need not come at the expense of another.”
The chair of the Apec senior officials’ meeting, Chen Xu, said Beijing had made trade “openness” a key focus of its Apec year and looked forward to “achieving more practical outcomes on the trade front”.
The much anticipated trilateral summit with Trump and Putin, on the other hand, could prove largely symbolic. For Xi, “it provides the appearance of China shaping the world order as an equal to the United States,” said Dr Kevork Oskanian, an expert on Russia at the University of Exeter. “Agreement on substantial issues, which would, in any case, require extensive preparatory negotiations, is unlikely.”
For China’s ruling Communist party, the political pomp has another key purpose. Nordin said summits were “occasions for leaders to tell stories about the world, about their country’s place in it … and one of the most important audiences for those stories is at home.”
For the locals watching the skyscraper light show on Monday night, the symbolism was not lost. China’s export might had helped it become increasingly powerful on the world stage, said one local man, who did not give his name. “It’s so great that the summit will take place in Shenzhen,” he said. “I feel very proud.”

articles.title_orig: Knesset votes 66-52 to elect Yashar’s Matan Kahana as speaker, in boost to Eisenkot bloc
articles.title_zh: Knesset votes 66-52 to elect Yashar’s Matan Kahana as speaker, in boost to Eisenkot bloc
articles.content_orig:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s grip on power suffered a critical blow on Tuesday as parliament voted to elect a new speaker, giving the opposition greater control over the legislative agenda.
The Knesset elected Matan Kahana of Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party as its 26th speaker, replacing Amir Ohana, from Netanyahu’s Likud party. Kahana received the support of 66 lawmakers, according to the Knesset spokesperson.
Lawmakers voted separately on the candidates, rather than in a head-to-head ballot. Likud’s candidate, coalition whip Ofir Katz, received the support of 52 lawmakers in a separate vote.
The vote marks the first significant move by the Eisenkot-led bloc to set a new direction for the legislature since Netanyahu lost his Knesset majority in the October 27 elections. The prime minister and his coalition of right-wing and ultra-Orthodox parties won only 53 seats in the 120-seat parliament. The opposition holds 67 seats, including 48 across four Jewish parties and a record 19 for two Arab parties: the Joint List and Raam.
Eisenkot, who was tasked by President Isaac Herzog earlier this month with forming the next government, has up to four and a half more weeks to replace Netanyahu, but his path to power remains difficult. However, his bloc now controls the Knesset plenum, key positions, and legislative agenda, and plans to use them to scrutinize and constrain Netanyahu’s caretaker government, which remains in office until it is replaced.
Eisenkot said Tuesday that Kahana’s appointment is a “proper democratic move which reflects the absolute majority who voted for change.”
Eisenkot’s bloc has already appointed interim chairs for key Knesset committees, including finance and defense, expanding oversight and control over the budget and strategic affairs. Avigdor Liberman, the leader of the opposition Yisrael Beitenu party now chairing the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, has already said he would summon all the security chiefs for briefings.
One of the opposition’s top legislative priorities is to undo judicial overhauls from Netanyahu’s outgoing coalition that sparked unprecedented nationwide protests in 2023. Critics of the overhaul said it weakened Israel’s democratic institutions and judicial oversight of the government.
Special committees have already been established to repeal a bill that changed how judges were selected and legislation that limits and weakens the attorney general. A separate committee was formed to undo a media regulation overhaul which expanded government control over the communications and news sector. Eisenkot’s bloc has also pledged to advance the establishment of a state commission of inquiry into the failures that led to the Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, which Netanyahu has refused to investigate.
Netanyahu and his allies tried to block Kahana’s election and to delegitimize it as dependent on the support of the Arab parties, even though they themselves have repeatedly sought support from Arab lawmakers in parliament. During the vote, members of Netanyahu’s bloc shouted “shame” at each Arab lawmaker who voted in support of Kahana.
Likud condemned the outcome after the vote, calling it “a low point in the history of the Knesset” and saying Kahana had been elected with the votes of what it called “terror supporters.”
While Eisenkot and his allies have seized control of the Knesset, his plan to replace Netanyahu still faces significant obstacles. Eisenkot wanted to form what he calls a “national emergency government,” a minority government made of the four Jewish opposition parties, which together hold 48 seats. The Arab parties would stay out of the coalition but would guarantee a majority in the Knesset to keep the government from collapsing in exchange for various concessions.
But other leaders in Eisenkot’s bloc are pushing in different directions. Liberman has vetoed any government that relies on the Arab parties’ support and is pushing for talks with the two ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism (UTJ), which have been traditionally allied with Netanyahu.
UTJ, the Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox party, declined to recommend Netanyahu for the premiership in the post-election consultations and has opened the door to informal talks with Eisenkot’s bloc. But it did not support Kahana in the vote for speaker of the Knesset, instead supporting Likud’s candidate. The second ultra-Orthodox party, Shas, remains loyal to Netanyahu, leaving Liberman’s strategy uncertain.
Another obstacle is former prime minister Naftali Bennett, who reportedly favors talks on a unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud party over an alliance with the Arab or ultra-Orthodox parties. However, Netanyahu has conditioned any talks on him remaining prime minister, which Eisenkot has rejected, raising doubts Bennett’s vision can succeed.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia says no longer shipping 'Hopper' AI chips to China
articles.title_zh: Nvidia says no longer shipping 'Hopper' AI chips to China
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia warned its customers that new legislation on Chinese companies remotely accessing its artificial-intelligence chips could expose it and them to U.S. "legal action," sources told CNBC.
The chip giant is facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips, which U.S. export controls restrict from going to China.
Nvidia messaged chip buyers in recent months to caution that the proposed Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services in the same way as physical hardware, potentially exposing both parties to legal risk, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The people asked not to be named while discussing private communications.
It also said that, for now, it would not sell its chips to customers who rent more than 50% of the graphics processing units, or GPUs, to Chinese companies, the people said.
Separately, the Financial Times reported earlier this month that Nvidia verbally told data-center clients to direct at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese customers under future contracts.
Regulators have had limited powers to control companies' access to those chips through cloud services hosted overseas.
RASA passed the House of Representatives in January but has not yet passed the Senate. Remote access to the chips has provoked the ire of President Donald Trump 's administration, which has sought to keep the chips out of China to maintain the U.S. lead in the AI race.
CNBC reported on Nov. 5 that Chinese lab Moonshot AI sought access to Nvidia chips through data centers in Europe. The Trump administration previously singled the company out, accusing it in July of accessing the chips through centers in East Asia.
The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced on Monday an interim final rule designed to prevent Chinese companies' remote access to AI chips.
Nvidia and BIS did not respond to a request for comment.
On Sunday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia after Jensen Huang 's shock departure as CEO, amid reports of an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. authorities reportedly suspect of spying for China.
Bessent suggested other Nvidia executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with export controls.
"I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent told Fox News.
In an August securities filing , Nvidia said it sought to "strictly comply with all applicable export control regulators" but did not have "physical control of our products after sale" and relied on its customers' and partners' compliance programs.
Huang has been asked to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.

articles.title_orig: China’s Xi pitches free trade at APEC amid Trump’s global trade disruptions
articles.title_zh: China’s Xi pitches free trade at APEC amid Trump’s global trade disruptions
articles.content_orig:
China’s President Xi Jinping has urged support for “free and open trade”, pitching Beijing as a stable partner – as opposed to President Donald Trump-led Washington – and pledging to stand up to trade protectionism.
Speaking on the sidelines of the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit on Wednesday in Shenzhen, southern China, Xi took aim at rising “unilateralism and protectionism”.
His remarks appeared to be a veiled criticism of Trump’s America First policies, under which the United States has imposed tariffs on both allies and economic rivals.
Xi is due to meet Trump, who is travelling from the Philippines for the APEC leaders’ summit later on Wednesday. Xi and Trump are then due to hold an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
On the sidelines of the APEC summit, Xi told business executives that the Asia Pacific must pursue more open trade and equitable growth to remain stable and dynamic.
Trump’s America First approach of tariff hikes and other moves runs counter to APEC’s aim of eventually forming a Pacific Rim free trade zone.
Washington also limits Chinese access to leading-edge US technology, such as the Nvidia computer chips that help power artificial intelligence (AI).
“We must firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, support free and open trade and investment, maintain the stability and smooth operation of global industrial and supply chains,” Xi said.
He added that China sought to “provide a more stable, predictable and beneficial environment for global enterprises” and would continue to expand access in its manufacturing and services sectors.
“Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access, and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform,” Xi said.
“While pursuing its own development, China has shared opportunities with other countries and worked for common development,” he said. “It has steadily brought stability and predictability to world economic growth and international trade and economic cooperation.”
George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, told the Associated Press news agency that Xi’s speech highlighted China’s aim to lead global industrial transformation.
“While he didn’t say so explicitly, his message was clear: China wants to be seen as a partner in global technology development, in contrast to Washington’s more restrictive approach,” Chen said, noting that Xi did not mention export controls, Nvidia, or the US directly.
Xi’s message is “likely to resonate with many Global South countries, and reinforces Beijing’s effort to contrast its technology strategy with that of Washington”, Chen added.

articles.title_orig: Record diesel prices drive UK inflation to 1-year high of 3.6%
articles.title_zh: Record diesel prices drive UK inflation to 1-year high of 3.6%
articles.content_orig:
U.K. inflation rose to 3.6% in the 12 months to October, its highest level in a year, as fuel costs continued to rise.
The reading was in line with the expectations of economists polled by Reuters and marked an increase from September's print of 3.5%.
October's reading puts U.K. inflation at a one-year high.
Britain's Office for National Statistics said the largest contributor to the rising inflation rate was motor fuel costs, which rose 33.2% year-on-year. It was the largest one-year rise in motor fuel prices since July 2022, when energy costs surged in the wake of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The U.K. is a net energy importer, making it vulnerable to external energy shocks such as the one sparked by the disruption of trade through the Strait of Hormuz.
Oil prices have retreated from their wartime highs of well above $100 a barrel, but remain elevated.
The ONS said Wednesday that the average price of petrol rose by 5.2 pence (7 cents) per liter between September and October this year, compared with a 0.7 pence per liter rise in the same period a year earlier. The average petrol price stood at 174.7 pence per liter in October, the highest it's been since Aug. 2022.
Diesel prices rose by 7 pence per liter in October, with the average price reaching 199.5 pence per liter — the highest since ONS records began in 1996.
The Iran war has seen energy costs surge in various major economies. U.S. diesel prices hit $6 per gallon for the first time ever in September.
Since the U.S.-Iran war began in late February, inflation has risen sharply after a brief dip thanks to an energy price cap that was revised upward in July.
Earlier this month, the Bank of England hiked interest rates for the first time in three years, warning that inflation could hit 5% by mid-2027.
Governor Andrew Bailey said in the bank's November Monetary Policy Report that without "real progress towards settling the conflict in the Middle East... risks to energy prices, and so to inflation, are to the upside."
Markets are currently pricing in around an 80% chance of a rate hike at the Bank of England's final meeting of the year.
Scott Gardner, investment strategist at JPMorgan Personal Investing, said in a note following the release that a recent climb down in oil prices following the U.S. midterm elections could offer some relief in future inflation readings.
But he added: "While this may be a short-term reprieve for motorists, the broader outlook for UK inflation remains challenging as we approach 2027. After hiking interest rates at the start of the month, the Bank will be wary of a sustained uptick in inflation that could be here to stay."

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
Framework announced its Wireless Touchpad Keyboard earlier this year with the goal of delivering a better couch keyboarding experience than the Logitech K400 . According to The Verge ’s Sean Hollister who went hands-on with Framework’s new all-in-one keyboard and touchpad last April, the company has succeeded in that goal, but it turns out you’ll be paying a bit more for Framework’s than Logitech’s.
While the K400 couch keyboard is $35, the Framework Wireless Touchpad Keyboard is $99 with a $50 fully refundable deposit required to preorder one starting today . That makes it nearly three times more expensive than Logitech’s, but Framework’s upgrades and improvements could make it worth the premium.
Instead of starting from scratch, Framework uses the same keyboard module found in its Laptop 12 paired with a precision 120Hz touchpad and controller that’s also used in all of the company’s computers. A Bluetooth connection is the easiest way to pair the keyboard to PCs running Windows, Linux, or macOS, or mobile devices, game consoles, and streaming boxes. You can quickly switch between four wirelessly connected devices with a button press including one that uses an included USB receiver. If you want more responsiveness, you can also tether it to a device with a USB-C cable.
On a full charge of its replaceable 1,200mAh battery the keyboard will run for well over a year with sporadic use. If you’re instead using it for hours every day on a desk, Framework estimates the battery life will be closer to over a month. For customizability and remapping the keyboard’s open source firmware is based on a fork of ZMK .
